ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَنَادَى أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ أَصْحَابَ النَّارِ أَنْ قَدْ وَجَدْنَا مَا وَعَدَنَا رَبُّنَا حَقًّا فَهَلْ وَجَدْتُمْ مَا وَعَدَ رَبُّكُمْ حَقًّا قَالُوا نَعَمْ فَأَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ بَيْنَهُمْ أَنْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ) (٤٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ قَدْ وَجَدْنَا): «أَنْ» may be in the sense of أَيْ (explicative "that is"), and it may be the lightened form (mukhaffafa) [of أَنَّ].
(حَقًّا): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it may be a second object, with وَجَدْنَا then in the sense of عَلِمْنَا ("we have known"). (مَا وَعَدَ رَبُّكُمْ): the object has been omitted from the second «وَعَدَ». So the implied form may be وَعَدَكُمْ ("He promised you"), and He omitted it because the first indicates it. The implied form may also be "what He promised the two parties", meaning our bliss and your punishment. And the implied form may be وَعَدَنَا ("He promised us"); what strengthens this is that what the people of the Fire are in is evil, and the verb used for that is أَوْعَدَ ("to threaten"), while وَعَدَ is used more often for good. (نَعَمْ): a particle with which a question is answered, affirming what was asked about. Its nūn and ʿayn are both with fatḥa; it is also read with kasra on the ʿayn, which is a dialect form; and it is permissible to put kasra on both of them by assimilation (itbāʿ). (بَيْنَهُمْ): it may be an adverb (ẓarf) of أَذَّنَ, and it may be a naʿt (adjective) of مُؤَذِّنٍ. (أَنْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ): it is read with fatḥa on the hamza and the nūn without shadda; it is the lightened form, i.e. "that it is that Allah has cursed him". It may also be in the sense of أَيْ, because the proclamation (al-adhān) is a saying. It is also read with shadda on the nūn and the accusative of اللَّعْنَة, and that is plain. In an irregular (shādhdh) reading it was read with kasra on the hamza, i.e. "and he said: أَنْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ". [Translator's note: the kasra reading would be إِنَّ / إِنْ, though the printed text repeats «أَنْ».]

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَيَبْغُونَهَا عِوَجًا وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ كَافِرُونَ) (٤٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَصُدُّونَ): it may be genitive, accusative or nominative.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَبَيْنَهُمَا حِجَابٌ وَعَلَى الْأَعْرَافِ رِجَالٌ يَعْرِفُونَ كُلًّا بِسِيمَاهُمْ وَنَادَوْا أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ أَنْ سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ لَمْ يَدْخُلُوهَا وَهُمْ يَطْمَعُونَ) (٤٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَنَادَوْا): the pronoun refers back to رِجَالٍ ("men"). (أَنْ سَلَامٌ): i.e. "that it is: peace"; and it may be in the sense of أَيْ (explicative "that is"). (لَمْ يَدْخُلُوهَا): i.e. the people of the Garden have not yet entered the Garden. (وَهُمْ يَطْمَعُونَ): in entering it; i.e. they called out to them in this state, and on this view the words «وَهُمْ يَطْمَعُونَ» have no grammatical position. It is also said: the meaning is that they called out to them after they had entered, but they entered it while they had not been hoping for it; on this view the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا صُرِفَتْ أَبْصَارُهُمْ تِلْقَاءَ أَصْحَابِ النَّارِ قَالُوا رَبَّنَا لَا تَجْعَلْنَا مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ) (٤٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تِلْقَاءَ): it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun). Among the maṣdars there is no tifʿāl — with kasra on the tāʾ — except تِلْقَاءٌ and تِبْيَانٌ; that pattern comes only in nouns, such as التِّمْثَالُ, التِّمْسَاحُ and التِّقْصَارُ. The accusative of «تِلْقَاءَ» here is as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "in the direction of the people of the Fire".

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَنَادَى أَصْحَابُ الْأَعْرَافِ رِجَالًا يَعْرِفُونَهُمْ بِسِيمَاهُمْ قَالُوا مَا أَغْنَى عَنْكُمْ جَمْعُكُمْ وَمَا كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ) (٤٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا أَغْنَى): «مَا» may be negating, and it may be interrogative.

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَهَؤُلَاءِ الَّذِينَ أَقْسَمْتُمْ لَا يَنَالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَا أَنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ) (٤٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَنَالُهُمُ): its implied form is "you swore concerning them that He would not reach them", so «لَا يَنَالُهُمُ» is the thing sworn to.
(ادْخُلُوا): its implied form is "so they turned to the people of the Garden and said: ادْخُلُوا (enter)". In an irregular (shādhdh) reading it is read وَادْخُلُوا [Translator's note: presumably the passive past "and they were made to enter", i.e. وَأُدْخِلُوا, as the following remark about "the declarative" indicates; the printed text gives «وَادْخُلُوا».] as a resumption, and that is said after they have entered. (لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمْ): if «ادْخُلُوا» is read as an imperative, the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "enter in safety"; and if it is read as a declarative (khabar), it is a turn from the third person to direct address.

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَنَادَى أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ أَنْ أَفِيضُوا عَلَيْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ أَوْ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَهُمَا عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ) (٥٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ أَفِيضُوا): «أَنْ» may be maṣdariyya (infinitival) or tafsīriyya (explicative). And (مِنَ الْمَاءِ): its implied form is "something of the water". (أَوْ مِمَّا): it is said that «أَوْ» is in the sense of the wāw ("and"), and His saying «حَرَّمَهُمَا» ("He has forbidden them both") was adduced as proof of that. It is also said: it is in its proper sense, and حَرَّمَهُمَا is according to the meaning, so there is an ellipsis in it, i.e. "each of them" or "both of them".

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَهُمْ لَهْوًا وَلَعِبًا وَغَرَّتْهُمُ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا فَالْيَوْمَ نَنْسَاهُمْ كَمَا نَسُوا لِقَاءَ يَوْمِهِمْ هَذَا وَمَا كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا يَجْحَدُونَ) (٥١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَهُمْ): it may be genitive, accusative or nominative. And (لَهْوًا): a second object, and the explanation is "a thing played with and a thing sported with". It may also be "they made their custom [a diversion]", because الدِّين has come in the sense of "custom" (al-ʿāda).

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ جِئْنَاهُمْ بِكِتَابٍ فَصَّلْنَاهُ عَلَى عِلْمٍ هُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ) (٥٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَى عِلْمٍ): it may be that "We detailed it as containing knowledge", so that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ. It may also be a ḥāl from the agent, i.e. "We detailed it knowing", i.e. on the basis of knowledge from Us.
(هُدًى وَرَحْمَةً): two ḥāls, i.e. "possessing guidance and possessing mercy". It was also read in the nominative, as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا تَأْوِيلَهُ يَوْمَ يَأْتِي تَأْوِيلُهُ يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ نَسُوهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ قَدْ جَاءَتْ رُسُلُ رَبِّنَا بِالْحَقِّ فَهَلْ لَنَا مِنْ شُفَعَاءَ فَيَشْفَعُوا لَنَا أَوْ نُرَدُّ فَنَعْمَلَ غَيْرَ الَّذِي كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ قَدْ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ) (٥٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَوْمَ يَأْتِي): it is an adverb (ẓarf) of «يَقُولُ». (فَيَشْفَعُوا لَنَا): it is accusative as the answer to the question. (أَوْ نُرَدُّ): the well-known reading is the nominative, and it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the position of «مِنْ شُفَعَاءَ», its implied form being "or will we be returned?". (فَنَعْمَلَ): also as the answer to the question. It is also read in the nominative, i.e. "so will we act?", and it then falls within the question. And the two of them are read in the accusative as the answer to the question.

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ يَطْلُبُهُ حَثِيثًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ وَالنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّرَاتٍ بِأَمْرِهِ أَلَا لَهُ الْخَلْقُ وَالْأَمْرُ تَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ) (٥٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ): there are two views on its position. One of them: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «خَلَقَ», and on this view the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ is «اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ». The second: it is resumptive. يُغْشِي is without shadda and with ḍamma on the yāʾ; it is from أَغْشَى, and it takes two objects, i.e. "Allah covers the night over the day". It is also read «يُغَشِّي» with shadda, and the meaning is the same. It is also read «يَغْشِي» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and without shadda, with اللَّيْلُ as its fāʿil (agent). (يَطْلُبُهُ): a ḥāl from اللَّيْل or from النَّهَار. And (حَثِيثًا): a ḥāl from اللَّيْل, because it is the agent.
It may also be from النَّهَار, so that the implied form is "the night seeks the day, being urged on"; and it may be a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a swift seeking". (وَالشَّمْسَ): it is read in the accusative, the implied form being "and He created the sun"; and whoever read the nominative began a new sentence.

ukberi-tibyan:55-55.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ادْعُوا رَبَّكُمْ تَضَرُّعًا وَخُفْيَةً إِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ) (٥٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَخُفْيَةً): it is read with ḍamma and with kasra on the khāʾ, and they are two dialect forms. The two maṣdars (verbal nouns) are ḥāls (circumstantials), and they may be a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). Similar to it is (خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا).

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ بَعْدَ إِصْلَاحِهَا وَادْعُوهُ خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا إِنَّ رَحْمَةَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ) (٥٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَرِيبٌ): it was not made feminine only because He meant the rain. It is also said: الرَّحْمَة and التَّرَحُّم have one meaning. It is also said: it is by way of relation (al-nasab), i.e. "possessing nearness", as one says امْرَأَةٌ طَالِقٌ ("a divorced woman"). It is also said: it is faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl, as they said لِحْيَةٌ دَهِينٌ ("an oiled beard") and كَفٌّ خَضِيبٌ ("a dyed palm"). It is also said: they meant the place, i.e. the place of Allah's mercy is near. It is also said: by dropping [the feminine marker] He distinguished between قَرِيب in the sense of kinship and قَرِيب in other senses.

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُرْسِلُ الرِّيَاحَ بُشْرًا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ حَتَّى إِذَا أَقَلَّتْ سَحَابًا ثِقَالًا سُقْنَاهُ لِبَلَدٍ مَيِّتٍ فَأَنْزَلْنَا بِهِ الْمَاءَ فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ كَذَلِكَ نُخْرِجُ الْمَوْتَى لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ) (٥٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بُشْرًا): it is read with nūn and with the shīn, both with ḍamma [i.e. نُشُرًا], and it is a plural. On its singular there are two views. One of them: نَشُورٌ, like صَبُورٌ and صُبُرٌ; on this view faʿūl may be in the sense of fāʿil, i.e. "reviving the earth", and it may be in the sense of mafʿūl, like رَكُوبٌ in the sense of مَرْكُوبٌ ("ridden"), i.e. "spread out" after folding, or "revived", i.e. "brought to life", from your saying أَنْشَرَ اللَّهُ الْمَيِّتَ فَهُوَ مُنْشَرٌ ("Allah revived the dead, so he is revived"). [The second:] it may be the plural of نَاشِرٌ, like نَازِلٌ and نُزُلٌ. It is also read with ḍamma on the nūn and sukūn on the shīn, by lightening the ḍamma-vowelled form. It is also read نَشْرًا with fatḥa on the nūn and sukūn on the shīn; it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of نَشَرَ ("he spread") after folding, or from your saying أَنْشَرَ اللَّهُ الْمَيِّتَ فَنُشِرَ, i.e. "he lived"; and its accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "spreading" or "possessing spreading", as you say جَاءَ رَكْضًا, i.e. رَاكِضًا ("he came running"). It is also read «بُشُرًا» with bāʾ and two ḍammas; it is the plural of بَشِيرٌ ("bearer of good news"), like قَلِيبٌ and قُلُبٌ. It is also read the same way except with sukūn on the shīn, for lightness; and similar to it in meaning is (يُرْسِلَ الرِّيَاحَ مُبَشِّرَاتٍ). It is also read «بُشْرَى», like حُبْلَى, i.e. "possessing good tidings". It is also read «بَشْرًا» with fatḥa on the bāʾ and sukūn on the shīn; it is the maṣdar of بَشَرْتُهُ, when you gave him good news. [Translator's note: the heading word printed as (بُشْرًا) does not match the first reading described, which is نُشُرًا with nūn.] (سَحَابًا): the plural of سَحَابَةٌ ("cloud"); and that is why He described it with the plural [ثِقَالًا]. (لِبَلَدٍ): i.e. "to revive a land". (بِهِ الْمَاءَ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of the bāʾ [Translator's note: so in the printed text; presumably «الْبَلَد», "the land", is meant.], or the pronoun of the clouds, or the pronoun of the wind; and likewise the hāʾ in the second «بِهِ».

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْبَلَدُ الطَّيِّبُ يَخْرُجُ نَبَاتُهُ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِ وَالَّذِي خَبُثَ لَا يَخْرُجُ إِلَّا نَكِدًا كَذَلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَشْكُرُونَ) (٥٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَخْرُجُ نَبَاتُهُ): it is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ, ḍamma on the rāʾ and the nominative of النَّبَات. It is also read the same way but with ḍamma on the yāʾ, as a passive (ʿalā mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu). And it is read with ḍamma on the yāʾ, kasra on the rāʾ and the accusative of النَّبَات, i.e. "so Allah brings out", or "the water". (بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَخْرُجُ. (إِلَّا نَكِدًا): with fatḥa on the nūn and kasra on the kāf; it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also read with fatḥa on both, as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "possessing hardship". It is also read with fatḥa on the nūn and sukūn on the kāf, and that too is a maṣdar; it is a dialect form. And «يُخْرِجُ» is read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ, with نَكِدًا as its object.

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَى قَوْمِهِ فَقَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ) (٥٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ): «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), «إِلَهٌ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لَكُمْ» is the khabar (predicate).
It is also said: the khabar is omitted, i.e. "you have no god in existence", and «لَكُمْ» is specification and clarification. As for «غَيْرُهُ» in the nominative, there are two views on it. One of them: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «إِلَهٍ» according to its position. The second: it is a badal (substitute) from the position, like لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ. It is also read in the accusative as an exception, and in the genitive as an adjective according to the wording. (عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ): the day is described as great, and what is meant is the greatness of what is in it.

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ إِنَّا لَنَرَاكَ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ) (٦٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ قَوْمِهِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْمَلَأ. And (نَرَاكَ): from seeing with the eye, so that (فِي ضَلَالٍ) is a ḥāl. It may also be from seeing with the heart (i.e. knowing), so that it is a second object.

ukberi-tibyan:61-62.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ لَيْسَ بِي ضَلَالَةٌ وَلَكِنِّي رَسُولٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٦١) أُبَلِّغُكُمْ رِسَالَاتِ رَبِّي وَأَنْصَحُ لَكُمْ وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ) (٦٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أُبَلِّغُكُمْ): it may be resumptive, and it may be a naʿt (adjective) of رَسُولٌ according to the meaning, because the messenger is the pronoun in «لَكِنِّي»; and had it been يُبَلِّغُكُمْ ("he conveys to you") it would have been permissible, because it would then refer back to the wording رَسُولٌ. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with the governing element in it being the preposition in His saying (مِنْ رَبِّ). (وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ اللَّهِ): in the sense of أَعْرِفُ ("I know"), so it takes one object, which is «مَا»; it is in the sense of الَّذِي, or an indefinite noun described [by what follows]. On مِنَ اللَّهِ there are two views. One of them: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَعْلَمُ, i.e. the beginning of my knowledge is from Allah. The second: it is a ḥāl from «مَا» or from the omitted resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid).

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَعَجِبْتُمْ أَنْ جَاءَكُمْ ذِكْرٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَلَى رَجُلٍ مِنْكُمْ لِيُنْذِرَكُمْ وَلِتَتَّقُوا وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ) (٦٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): it may be a naʿt (adjective) of (ذِكْرٌ), and it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to جَاءَكُمْ.
(عَلَى رَجُلٍ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ذِكْرٌ, i.e. "sent down upon a man", and it may be attached to جَاءَكُمْ according to the meaning, because it carries the meaning of "sent down to you". In the speech there is the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "upon the heart of a man" or "the tongue of a man".

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَنْجَيْنَاهُ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ فِي الْفُلْكِ وَأَغْرَقْنَا الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَوْمًا عَمِينَ) (٦٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي الْفُلْكِ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الَّذِينَ» or from the nominative pronoun in مَعَهُ. The origin of (عَمِينَ) is عَمِيِينَ; the first [yāʾ] was given sukūn and dropped.

ukberi-tibyan:65-65.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِلَى عَادٍ أَخَاهُمْ هُودًا قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ) (٦٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هُودًا): a badal (substitute) from أَخَاهُمْ, and أَخَاهُمْ is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and We sent to ʿĀd"; and likewise the beginnings of the stories that come after it.

ukberi-tibyan:193-193.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَى الْهُدَى لَا يَتَّبِعُوكُمْ سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ أَدَعَوْتُمُوهُمْ أَمْ أَنْتُمْ صَامِتُونَ) (١٩٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَدَعَوْتُمُوهُمْ): this has been discussed under His saying: (سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ).
And (أَمْ أَنْتُمْ صَامِتُونَ): a nominal clause in the position of a verbal clause; the implied wording is: أَدَعَوْتُمُوهُمْ أَمْ صَمَتُّمْ ("whether you called them or kept silent").

ukberi-tibyan:194-194.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ عِبَادٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ فَادْعُوهُمْ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ) (١٩٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ): the majority read it with the nūn doubled (tashdīd); and (عِبَادٌ) is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ. And (أَمْثَالُكُمْ) is a naʿt (adjective) to it, and the returning pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. تَدْعُو بِهِمْ. It is also read «عِبَادًا», and it is then a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted returning pronoun, with أَمْثَالُكُمُ as the khabar. And «إِنْ» is read without doubling, in which case it has the meaning of «مَا» ("not"), and عِبَادًا is its khabar, and «أَمْثَالَكُمْ» is read in the accusative as a naʿt to عِبَادًا. It has also been read «أَمْثَالُكُمْ» in the nominative, on the basis that عِبَادًا is a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun and «أَمْثَالُكُمْ» is the khabar. And إِنْ in the meaning of «مَا» does not govern according to Sībawayh, and does govern according to al-Mubarrad.

ukberi-tibyan:195-195.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَهُمْ أَرْجُلٌ يَمْشُونَ بِهَا أَمْ لَهُمْ أَيْدٍ يَبْطِشُونَ بِهَا أَمْ لَهُمْ أَعْيُنٌ يُبْصِرُونَ بِهَا أَمْ لَهُمْ آذَانٌ يَسْمَعُونَ بِهَا قُلِ ادْعُوا شُرَكَاءَكُمْ ثُمَّ كِيدُونِ فَلَا تُنْظِرُونِ) (١٩٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قُلِ ادْعُوا): it is read with ḍamma on the lām and with kasra; we have mentioned this under His saying: (فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ).

ukberi-tibyan:196-196.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ وَلِيِّيَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ الْكِتَابَ وَهُوَ يَتَوَلَّى الصَّالِحِينَ) (١٩٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ وَلِيِّيَ اللَّهُ): the majority read it with the first yāʾ doubled and the second with fatḥa, and this is the original form. It is also read with the second [yāʾ] dropped in pronunciation, because it is vowelless and what follows it is vowelless; and it is read with fatḥa on the first yāʾ and no yāʾ after it, the second being dropped from pronunciation for lightness.

ukberi-tibyan:201-201.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا فَإِذَا هُمْ مُبْصِرُونَ) (٢٠١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (طَيْفٌ): it is read with the yāʾ undoubled, and there are two views about it. The first: its origin is طَيِّفٌ, like مَيِّتٍ, and it was lightened. The second: it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of طَافَ يَطِيفُ, said when something encompasses a thing. It is also said: it is the maṣdar of يَطُوفُ, the wāw being changed into yāʾ although it is vowelless, just as it was changed in أَيْدٍ; but this is far-fetched. And it is read طَائِفٌ, on the pattern fāʿil.

ukberi-tibyan:202-202.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِخْوَانُهُمْ يَمُدُّونَهُمْ فِي الْغَيِّ ثُمَّ لَا يُقْصِرُونَ) (٢٠٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَمُدُّونَهُمْ): with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the mīm, from مَدَّ يَمُدُّ, like His saying: (وَيَمُدُّهُمْ فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ); and it is read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the mīm, from أَمَدَّهُ إِمْدَادًا. (فِي الْغَيِّ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb mentioned, and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object pronoun or from the agent pronoun.

ukberi-tibyan:204-204.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا قُرِئَ الْقُرْآنُ فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وَأَنْصِتُوا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ) (٢٠٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ): the lām may be in the meaning of "for Allah" (لِلَّهِ), i.e. "for its sake" (لِأَجْلِهِ); it may be redundant (zāʾida), i.e. فَاسْتَمِعُوهُ ("so listen to it"); and it may be in the meaning of إِلَى ("to").

ukberi-tibyan:205-205.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ فِي نَفْسِكَ تَضَرُّعًا وَخِيفَةً وَدُونَ الْجَهْرِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصَالِ وَلَا تَكُنْ مِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ) (٢٠٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَضَرُّعًا وَخِيفَةً): two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also said: it is a maṣdar of a verb not from the [root] mentioned but from its meaning. (وَدُونَ الْجَهْرِ): conjoined (maʿṭūf) to تَضَرُّع, and the implied sense is: "moderate" (مُقْتَصِدِينَ). (بِالْغُدُوِّ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to اذْكُرْ. (وَالْآصَالِ): a plural of a plural, because the singular is أَصِيلٌ, and faʿīl is not pluralised on afʿāl but on fuʿul, and then fuʿul is pluralised on afʿāl; the origin is أَصِيلٌ and أَصْلٌ «[Translator's note: so vocalised in the text; the fuʿul form just described would be أُصُلٌ]», then آصَالٌ.
It is read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, وَالْإِيصَالِ, with kasra on the hamza and a yāʾ after it; this is the maṣdar of آصَلْنَا, said when we enter the time of al-aṣīl (late afternoon).
My Lord, make it easy (رب يسر).

ukberi-tibyan:68-68.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُبَلِّغُكُمْ رِسَالَاتِ رَبِّي وَأَنَا لَكُمْ نَاصِحٌ أَمِينٌ) (٦٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَاصِحٌ أَمِينٌ): it [أَمِينٌ] is faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl (passive participle).

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَعَجِبْتُمْ أَنْ جَاءَكُمْ ذِكْرٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَلَى رَجُلٍ مِنْكُمْ لِيُنْذِرَكُمْ وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ جَعَلَكُمْ خُلَفَاءَ مِنْ بَعْدِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَزَادَكُمْ فِي الْخَلْقِ بَسْطَةً فَاذْكُرُوا آلَاءَ اللَّهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ) (٦٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي الْخَلْقِ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بَسْطَةً», and it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to زَادَكُمْ. الْآلَاءُ ("the favours") is a plural, and on its singular there are three dialect forms: إِلًى — with kasra on the hamza and a single alif after the lām; the same with fatḥa on the hamza [أَلًى]; and with kasra on the hamza, sukūn on the lām and a yāʾ after it [إِلْيٌ].

ukberi-tibyan:70-70.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا أَجِئْتَنَا لِنَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ وَحْدَهُ وَنَذَرَ مَا كَانَ يَعْبُدُ آبَاؤُنَا فَأْتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَا إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ) (٧٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَحْدَهُ): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) with its augment letters dropped. On its position there are two views. One of them: it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from اللَّه, i.e. "that we should worship Allah as singled out and declared one"; and some of them said: it is a ḥāl from the agents, i.e. "declaring His oneness". The second: it is an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "that we should worship Allah [alone] as He is"; Yūnus said this. The origin of this maṣdar is الْإِيحَادُ, from your saying أَوْحَدْتُهُ ("I singled him out"); the hamza and the alif were dropped, and they are the two augments.

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ قَدْ وَقَعَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ رِجْسٌ وَغَضَبٌ أَتُجَادِلُونَنِي فِي أَسْمَاءٍ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنْتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمْ مَا نَزَّلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ فَانْتَظِرُوا إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُنْتَظِرِينَ) (٧١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رِجْسٌ», and it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to وَقَعَ.
(فِي أَسْمَاءٍ): i.e. "about possessors of names", or "about things named".

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِلَى ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَالِحًا قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ قَدْ جَاءَتْكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ هَذِهِ نَاقَةُ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ آيَةً فَذَرُوهَا تَأْكُلْ فِي أَرْضِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تَمَسُّوهَا بِسُوءٍ فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ) (٧٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (آيَةً): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from النَّاقَة, and the governing element in it is the meaning of drawing attention and pointing contained in «هَذِهِ».
It is also permissible that «لَكُمْ» governs «آيَةً»; and it is permissible that لَكُمْ is a ḥāl from «آيَةً»; and it is permissible that «نَاقَةُ اللَّهِ» is a badal (substitute) from هَذِهِ or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), with «لَكُمْ» as the khabar (predicate). It is permissible for «آيَةً» to be a ḥāl because it is in the sense of «a sign and a proof». (تَأْكُلْ): the answer to the command. (فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ): the answer to the prohibition. It was also read in the nominative, and its position is a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ جَعَلَكُمْ خُلَفَاءَ مِنْ بَعْدِ عَادٍ وَبَوَّأَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ تَتَّخِذُونَ مِنْ سُهُولِهَا قُصُورًا وَتَنْحِتُونَ الْجِبَالَ بُيُوتًا فَاذْكُرُوا آلَاءَ اللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ) (٧٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ سُهُولِهَا): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قُصُورًا», [it may be] a second object of «تَتَّخِذُونَ», and it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَتَّخِذُونَ, not on the basis that «تَتَّخِذُونَ» takes two objects but rather one. And (مِنْ) is for the beginning of the extent of the taking. (وَتَنْحِتُونَ الْجِبَالَ): there are two views on it. One of them: it is in the sense of تَتَّخِذُونَ, so that «بُيُوتًا» is a second object. The second: the implied form is "from the mountains", in accordance with what came in the other verse, so that بُيُوتًا is the object, and "from the mountains" is as we mentioned for His saying «مِنْ سُهُولِهَا».

ukberi-tibyan:75-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ لِلَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا لِمَنْ آمَنَ مِنْهُمْ أَتَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ صَالِحًا مُرْسَلٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ قَالُوا إِنَّا بِمَا أُرْسِلَ بِهِ مُؤْمِنُونَ) (٧٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِمَنْ آمَنَ): it is a badal (substitute) from His saying «لِلَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا», with the preposition repeated, as in your saying مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ بِأَخِيكَ ("I passed by Zayd, by your brother").

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دَارِهِمْ جَاثِمِينَ) (٧٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَأَصْبَحُوا): it may be the complete (tāmma) verb, with «جَاثِمِينَ» a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it may be the incomplete (nāqiṣa) one, with جَاثِمِينَ the khabar (predicate); and فِي دَارِهِمْ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «جَاثِمِينَ».

ukberi-tibyan:81-81.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ولوطا إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ أتأتون الْفَاحِشَة مَا سبقكم بهَا من أحد من الْعَالمين إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ الرِّجَالَ شَهْوَةً مِنْ دُونِ النِّسَاءِ بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُسْرِفُونَ) (٨١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلُوطًا): i.e. "and We sent Lūṭ", or "and remember Lūṭ". And (إِذْ): on the first implied form it is an adverb (ẓarf), and on the second it is an adverb of an omitted element, whose implied form is "and remember the mission of Lūṭ when…". (مَا سَبَقَكُمْ بِهَا): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْفَاحِشَة, or from the agent in «أَتَأْتُونَ», its implied form being "initiating [it]". (أَئِنَّكُمْ): it is read with two hamzas as a question; it is permissible to lighten the second and to soften it, which is to make it between the yāʾ and the alif. It is also read with a single hamza as a statement (khabar). (شَهْوَةً): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl. (مِنْ دُونِ النِّسَاءِ): a naʿt (adjective) of رِجَالٍ, i.e. "apart from women". (بَلْ أَنْتُمْ): بَلْ here is for passing from one story to another. It is also said: it is a turning away (iḍrāb) from an omitted element, its implied form being "you have not acted justly; rather you are transgressors".

ukberi-tibyan:82-82.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوا أَخْرِجُوهُمْ مِنْ قَرْيَتِكُمْ إِنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ) (٨٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِ): it is read in the accusative and the nominative. It has been mentioned in Āl ʿImrān and in al-Anʿām.

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ مَطَرًا فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ) (٨٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَطَرًا): it is the object of أَمْطَرْنَا, and the "rain" here is stones, as came in the other verse: (وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ حِجَارَةً).

ukberi-tibyan:85-85.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِلَى مَدْيَنَ أَخَاهُمْ شُعَيْبًا قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ قَدْ جَاءَتْكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَأَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ وَالْمِيزَانَ وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا النَّاسَ أَشْيَاءَهُمْ وَلَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ بَعْدَ إِصْلَاحِهَا ذَلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) (٨٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا): it takes two objects, namely «النَّاسَ» and «أَشْيَاءَهُمْ». You say بَخَسْتُ زَيْدًا حَقَّهُ, i.e. "I diminished Zayd his due".

ukberi-tibyan:86-86.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَقْعُدُوا بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ تُوعِدُونَ وَتَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ مَنْ آمَنَ بِهِ وَتَبْغُونَهَا عِوَجًا وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ كُنْتُمْ قَلِيلًا فَكَثَّرَكُمْ وَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُفْسِدِينَ) (٨٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تُوعِدُونَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in تَقْعُدُوا. (مَنْ آمَنَ): the object of تَصُدُّونَ, not the object of تُوعِدُونَ, since if it were the object of the first, it would have been تَصُدُّونَهُمْ. (وَتَبْغُونَهَا): a ḥāl. We have mentioned it at His saying, Exalted is He: (يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لِمَ تَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) in Āl ʿImrān.

ukberi-tibyan:88-88.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ لَنُخْرِجَنَّكَ يَا شُعَيْبُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَكَ مِنْ قَرْيَتِنَا أَوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ فِي مِلَّتِنَا قَالَ أَوَلَوْ كُنَّا كَارِهِينَ) (٨٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوَلَوْ كُنَّا كَارِهِينَ): i.e. "even if we dislike it, will you bring us back?". «وَلَوْ» here is in the sense of إِنْ ("if"), because it is the future [Translator's note: the printed text reads «الْمُسْتَقِيلُ», evidently for «الْمُسْتَقْبَلُ», "the future"; the gloss إِنَّ is likewise printed with shadda.]. It may also be in its original sense, the meaning being "if we are unwilling in this state".

ukberi-tibyan:89-89.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدِ افْتَرَيْنَا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا إِنْ عُدْنَا فِي مِلَّتِكُمْ بَعْدَ إِذْ نَجَّانَا اللَّهُ مِنْهَا وَمَا يَكُونُ لَنَا أَنْ نَعُودَ فِيهَا إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ رَبُّنَا وَسِعَ رَبُّنَا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا عَلَى اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْنَا رَبَّنَا افْتَحْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْفَاتِحِينَ) (٨٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَدِ افْتَرَيْنَا): it is in the sense of the future, because it has not happened; it only takes the place of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of «إِنْ عُدْنَا». The entry of قَدْ here is acceptable because they treated the fabrication upon returning as something that has occurred, so they joined it with قَدْ; it is as if the meaning were "we have fabricated now, if we resolve to return". (إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ): the maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of an accusative as an exception, and the implied form is "except at the time that Allah wills". It is also said: it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). It is also said: "except in the state of Allah's willing". And (عِلْمًا): it has been mentioned in al-Anʿām.

ukberi-tibyan:90-90.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ لَئِنِ اتَّبَعْتُمْ شُعَيْبًا إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا لَخَاسِرُونَ) (٩٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذًا لَخَاسِرُونَ): «إِذًا» here is placed in the middle between the noun of إِنَّ and its khabar (predicate). It is a particle whose meaning is a reply, and it governs the verb under particular conditions; but this is not its [governing] position.

ukberi-tibyan:92-92.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا شُعَيْبًا كَأَنْ لَمْ يَغْنَوْا فِيهَا الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا شُعَيْبًا كَانُوا هُمُ الْخَاسِرِينَ) (٩٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا شُعَيْبًا): you have three views on it. The first of them: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and on the khabar (predicate) there are two views. One of them: [the khabar is] كَأَنْ لَمْ يَغْنَوْا فِيهَا, and what follows it is another clause, or a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in يَغْنَوْا, or an accusative by implying أَعْنِي ("I mean"). The second: that the khabar is «الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا شُعَيْبًا كَانُوا», and on this view (كَأَنْ لَمْ يَغْنَوْا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in كَذَّبُوا. The second view: it is a naʿt (adjective) of His saying (الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ). The third: it is a badal from it; and on both views «كَأَنْ لَمْ» is a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:95-95.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ بَدَّلْنَا مَكَانَ السَّيِّئَةِ الْحَسَنَةَ حَتَّى عَفَوْا وَقَالُوا قَدْ مَسَّ آبَاءَنَا الضَّرَّاءُ وَالسَّرَّاءُ فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ) (٩٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَتَّى عَفَوْا): i.e. "until they abounded", i.e. they became many.
(فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to عَفَوْا.

ukberi-tibyan:98-98.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أفأمن أهل الْقرى أَن يَأْتِيهم بأسنا بياتا وهم نائمون أَوَأَمِنَ أَهْلُ الْقُرَى أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ بَأْسُنَا ضُحًى وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ) (٩٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوَأَمِنَ أَهْلُ الْقُرَى): it is read with fatḥa on the wāw, as the conjunctive wāw on which the interrogative hamza has entered. It is also read with sukūn on it [أَوْ], and it is then for one of two things; the meaning is: "did they then feel secure from the punishment coming in the forenoon, or feel secure from its coming to them at night?". And (بَيَاتًا): the ḥāl (circumstantial) from بَأْسُنَا, i.e. "coming in secret to take them unawares by night". [Translator's note: the word بَيَاتًا actually occurs in the preceding verse (97).]

ukberi-tibyan:99-99.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَأَمِنُوا مَكْرَ اللَّهِ فَلَا يَأْمَنُ مَكْرَ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ) (٩٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَلَا يَأْمَنُ مَكْرَ اللَّهِ): the fāʾ here is to draw attention to the punishment following immediately upon «أَمِنَ مَكْرَ اللَّهِ» ("feeling secure from Allah's plan").

ukberi-tibyan:100-100.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لِلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِ أَهْلِهَا أَنْ لَوْ نَشَاءُ أَصَبْنَاهُمْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَنَطْبَعُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يَسْمَعُونَ) (١٠٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لِلَّذِينَ): it is read with the yāʾ, and its fāʿil (agent) is «أَنْ لَوْ نَشَاءُ»; أَنْ is lightened from the heavy [أَنَّ], i.e. "has their knowledge of Our will not made clear to them?". It is also read with the nūn [نَهْدِ], and أَنْ لَوْ نَشَاءُ is its object. It is also said: the agent of يَهْدِي is the pronoun of the name of Allah the Exalted. (فَهُمْ لَا يَسْمَعُونَ): the fāʾ is for the non-hearing following upon the sealing of the heart without any interval.

ukberi-tibyan:101-101.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تِلْكَ الْقُرَى نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَائِهَا وَلَقَدْ جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَمَا كَانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا بِمَا كَذَّبُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ كَذَلِكَ يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِ الْكَافِرِينَ) (١٠١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَائِهَا): it is like His saying (ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ), and it has been mentioned in Āl ʿImrān; and like His saying, Exalted is He: (تِلْكَ آيَاتُ اللَّهِ نَتْلُوهَا), and it has been mentioned in al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:102-102.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا وَجَدْنَا لِأَكْثَرِهِمْ مِنْ عَهْدٍ وَإِنْ وَجَدْنَا أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَفَاسِقِينَ) (١٠٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِأَكْثَرِهِمْ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «عَهْدٍ». And مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "We did not find a covenant for most of them".
(وَإِنْ وَجَدْنَا): [إِنْ] is lightened from the heavy [إِنَّ], and its noun is omitted, i.e. "and indeed We found". The lām in «لَفَاسِقِينَ» is obligatory with it, to distinguish between the lightened أَنْ [Translator's note: so printed; the lightened إِنْ is meant.] and إِنْ in the sense of «مَا» ("not"). The Kufans said: [it is not] from the heavy [form]; it is «إِنْ» in the sense of «مَا» [and the lām is in the sense of إِلَّا]. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «مِنَ الثَّقِيلَةِ "إِنْ" بِمَعْنَى "مَا"», apparently with words dropped; translated according to the known Kufan position.] It has been mentioned in al-Baqara at His saying (وَإِنْ كَانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةً).

ukberi-tibyan:103-103.t:
قَالَ تَعَالَى {ثمَّ بعثنَا من بعدهمْ مُوسَى بِآيَاتِنَا إِلَى فِرْعَوْن وملئه فظلموا بهَا فَانْظُر كَيفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَة المفسدين}
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَيْفَ كَانَ): كَيْفَ is in the accusative position as the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ. (عَاقِبَةُ): its noun; and the clause is in the accusative position by «فَانْظُرْ».

ukberi-tibyan:105-105.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حَقِيقٌ عَلَى أَنْ لَا أَقُولَ عَلَى اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْحَقَّ قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِبَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعِيَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ) (١٠٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَقِيقٌ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is «أَنْ لَا أَقُولَ», on the reading of whoever put shadda on the yāʾ in «عَلَيَّ»; and «عَلَيَّ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «حَقِيقٌ». The better view is that «أَنْ لَا» is the fāʿil (agent) of «حَقِيقٌ», because it stands in for حَقٌّ عَلَيَّ ("it is incumbent on me"). It is also read عَلَى إِلَّا [Translator's note: so printed; the reading meant is عَلَى أَنْ لَا, without the yāʾ of the first person.], and the meaning is "bound to not say". On the correct view حَقِيقٌ here is a naʿt (adjective) of رَسُولٌ, or a second khabar, as you say أَنَا حَقِيقٌ بِكَذَا, i.e. "I am most worthy of such-and-such". It is also said: the meaning on the reading of whoever put shadda on the yāʾ is that «حَقِيقٌ» is a naʿt of رَسُولٌ, and what follows it is a mubtadaʾ and khabar; i.e. [I am bound] to saying the truth.

ukberi-tibyan:107-107.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَلْقَى عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُبِينٌ) (١٠٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِذَا هِيَ): «إِذَا» is for surprise (al-mufājaʾa), and it is [an adverb of] place; what follows it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (ثُعْبَانٌ) is its khabar (predicate). It is also said: it is an adverb of time. We have treated it fully in what preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:110-111.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ. قَالُوا أرجه وأخاه وَأرْسل فِي الْمَدَائِن حاشرين).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ): it is like His saying (مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ), and it has been mentioned in al-Baqara. On the meaning there are two views. One of them: it is the completion of the report of what the chiefs (al-malaʾ) said. The second: it is resumptive, from what Pharaoh said, its implied form being "so he said: what do you command?"; what follows indicates this, namely His saying «قَالُوا أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ». And «أَرْجِئْهُ»: it is read with the hamza and with ḍamma on the hāʾ without lengthening (ishbāʿ), and that is the good reading; and with lengthening, which is weak, because the hāʾ is faint, so it is as if the wāw after it followed directly on the [vowelless] hamza, which is close to joining two vowelless letters; and for this reason their saying عَلَيْهِ مَالٌ with lengthening is considered weak.
It is also read with kasra on the hāʾ together with the hamza, and that is weak, because the hamza is a sound, vowelless letter, so there is nothing before the hāʾ that requires the kasra. Its justification is that he made the hāʾ follow the kasra of the jīm, the barrier [between them] not being a strong one.
It is also read without hamza, from أَرْجَيْتُ with the yāʾ; then some of them put kasra on the hāʾ and lengthen it, some do not lengthen it, and some give it sukūn. We have explained that at (يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ).

ukberi-tibyan:112-112.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ سَاحِرٍ عَلِيمٍ) (١١٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِكُلِّ سَاحِرٍ): it is read with an alif after the sīn, and [also] with an alif after the ḥāʾ together with shadda [سَحَّارٍ], and that is the more common.

ukberi-tibyan:113-113.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَاءَ السَّحَرَةُ فِرْعَوْنَ قَالُوا إِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجْرًا إِنْ كُنَّا نَحْنُ الْغَالِبِينَ) (١١٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَئِنَّ لَنَا): it is read with two hamzas as a question, with full pronunciation (taḥqīq) and with softening (talyīn), as preceded; and with a single hamza as a statement (khabar).

ukberi-tibyan:115-115.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا يَا مُوسَى إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّا أَنْ نَكُونَ نَحْنُ الْمُلْقِينَ) (١١٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ): on the position of أَنْ and the verb there are two views.
One of them: nominative, i.e. "our matter is either the throwing". The second: accusative, i.e. "either you do the throwing".

ukberi-tibyan:116-116.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ أَلْقُوا فَلَمَّا أَلْقَوْا سَحَرُوا أَعْيُنَ النَّاسِ وَاسْتَرْهَبُوهُمْ وَجَاءُوا بِسِحْرٍ عَظِيمٍ) (١١٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاسْتَرْهَبُوهُمْ): i.e. they sought to terrify them. It is also said: it is in the sense of أَرْهَبُوهُمْ ("they terrified them"), like قَرَّ and اسْتَقَرَّ.

ukberi-tibyan:117-117.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسَى أَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ) (١١٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ أَلْقِ): أَنْ may be the maṣdariyya (infinitival) one, and it may be in the sense of أَيْ (explicative "that is"). (فَإِذَا هِيَ تَلْقَفُ): it is read with fatḥa on the lām and shadda on the qāf, with the tāʾ without shadda, like تَكَلَّمَ. It is also read «تَّلَقَّفُ», likewise with shadda on the qāf; the origin is تَتَلَقَّفُ, and the first [tāʾ] was assimilated into the second, and it was joined to what precedes it, so that this made the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) unnecessary. And it is read with sukūn on the lām and fatḥa on the qāf [تَلْقَفُ], its past being لَقِفَ, like عَلِمَ.

ukberi-tibyan:121-121.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ) (١٢١) (رَبِّ مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ) (١٢٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَالُوا آمَنَّا): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "so they turned back humbled, having said…". It may also be resumptive. (رَبِّ مُوسَى): a badal (substitute) from what precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:123-123.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ آذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّ هَذَا لَمَكْرٌ مَكَرْتُمُوهُ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ لِتُخْرِجُوا مِنْهَا أَهْلَهَا فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ) (١٢٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ آمَنْتُمْ): it is read with two hamzas as a question; some of them pronounce the second fully, and some of them lighten it. Separating the two with an alif is far-fetched, because in the underlying form it would become like four alifs.
It is also read with a single hamza in the form of a statement (khabar); it may then be a statement in meaning, or the interrogative hamza may have been dropped.
And it was read «فِرْعَوْنُ وَأَمَنْتُمْ», by turning the first hamza into a wāw because what precedes it has ḍamma.

ukberi-tibyan:126-126.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا تَنْقِمُ مِنَّا إِلَّا أَنْ آمَنَّا بِآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا لَمَّا جَاءَتْنَا رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا وَتَوَفَّنَا مُسْلِمِينَ) (١٢٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا تَنْقِمُ): it is read with kasra and with fatḥa on the qāf, and it has been mentioned in al-Māʾida.

ukberi-tibyan:127-127.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْ قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ أَتَذَرُ مُوسَى وَقَوْمَهُ لِيُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَيَذَرَكَ وَآلِهَتَكَ قَالَ سَنُقَتِّلُ أَبْنَاءَهُمْ وَنَسْتَحْيِي نِسَاءَهُمْ وَإِنَّا فَوْقَهُمْ قَاهِرُونَ) (١٢٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَذَرَكَ): the majority read fatḥa on the rāʾ, as conjoined to لِيُفْسِدُوا; some of them gave it sukūn for lightness, and some of them gave it ḍamma, i.e. "while he leaves you". It is also read «وَإِلَاهَتَكَ» [Translator's note: the printed text has «وَإِلَهَتَكَ».], [on the pattern] like الْعِبَادَة and الزِّيَارَة, and it means worship.

ukberi-tibyan:128-128.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ اسْتَعِينُوا بِاللَّهِ وَاصْبِرُوا إِنَّ الْأَرْضَ لِلَّهِ يُورِثُهَا مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ) (١٢٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُورِثُهَا): it may be resumptive, and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «اللَّه».

ukberi-tibyan:130-130.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْنَا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ بِالسِّنِينَ وَنَقْصٍ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ) (١٣٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِالسِّنِينَ): the origin of سَنَةٌ is سَنَهَةٌ, so its final radical (lām) is a hāʾ, because of their saying عَامَلْتُهُ مُسَانَهَةً ("I dealt with him by the year"). It is also said: its final radical is a wāw, because of their saying سَنَوَاتٌ. Most of the Arabs treat it like «الزَّيْدُونَ» [i.e. as a sound masculine plural], and some of them make the nūn the inflected letter. Its sīn was given kasra to signal that it was pluralised irregularly. (مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to نَقْصٍ, and the meaning is "and by the diminishing of fruits".

ukberi-tibyan:131-131.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِذَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْحَسَنَةُ قَالُوا لَنَا هَذِهِ وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَطَّيَّرُوا بِمُوسَى وَمَنْ مَعَهُ أَلَا إِنَّمَا طَائِرُهُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ) (١٣٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَطَّيَّرُوا): i.e. يَتَطَيَّرُوا ("they ascribe ill omen"). In an irregular reading (shādhdh) it was read «تَطَيَّرُوا» in the form of the past.
(طَائِرُهُمْ): in the form of the singular; and it is read طَيْرُهُمْ. Something similar has been mentioned in Āl ʿImrān.

ukberi-tibyan:132-132.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالُوا مَهْمَا تَأْتِنَا بِهِ مِنْ آيَةٍ لِتَسْحَرَنَا بِهَا فَمَا نَحْنُ لَكَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ) (١٣٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَهْمَا): on it there are three opinions. The first of them: «مَهْ» is in the sense of "desist!", and «مَا» is a conditional noun, as in His saying (مَا يَفْتَحِ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ مِنْ رَحْمَةٍ). The second: the origin of «مَهْ» is the conditional مَا, to which مَا was added, as it was added in His saying (فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ); then the first alif was replaced by hāʾ, so that two words of one form would not follow each other.
The third: it is, as a whole, a single word that is not compound. On all the opinions the position of the noun is accusative by «تَأْتِينَا», and the hāʾ in «بِهِ» refers back to that noun.

ukberi-tibyan:133-133.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ الطُّوفَانَ وَالْجَرَادَ وَالْقُمَّلَ وَالضَّفَادِعَ وَالدَّمَ آيَاتٍ مُفَصَّلَاتٍ فَاسْتَكْبَرُوا وَكَانُوا قَوْمًا مُجْرِمِينَ) (١٣٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الطُّوفَانَ): it is said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); and it is said that it is the plural of طُوفَانَةٌ; it is the abundant, drowning water. (وَالْجَرَادَ): the plural of جَرَادَةٌ, male and female being alike. (وَالْقُمَّلَ): it is read with shadda, and without shadda with fatḥa on the qāf and sukūn on the mīm [الْقَمْلَ]. It is said: they are two dialect forms. It is also said: they [the latter] are the well-known lice in clothes and the like, while the one with shadda occurs in food. (آيَاتٍ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the things mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:134-134.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا وَقَعَ عَلَيْهِمُ الرِّجْزُ قَالُوا يَا مُوسَى ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ بِمَا عَهِدَ عِنْدَكَ لَئِنْ كَشَفْتَ عَنَّا الرِّجْزَ لَنُؤْمِنَنَّ لَكَ وَلَنُرْسِلَنَّ مَعَكَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ) (١٣٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِمَا عَهِدَ عِنْدَكَ): the bāʾ may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to ادْعُ, i.e. "by the thing with which Allah taught you to supplicate"; and the bāʾ may be for the oath.

ukberi-tibyan:135-135.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمُ الرِّجْزَ إِلَى أَجَلٍ هُمْ بَالِغُوهُ إِذَا هُمْ يَنْكُثُونَ) (١٣٥).
(إِذَا هُمْ يَنْكُثُونَ): هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), يَنْكُثُونَ is the khabar (predicate), and إِذَا is for surprise (al-mufājaʾa); its mention has preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:137-137.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَوْرَثْنَا الْقَوْمَ الَّذِينَ كَانُوا يُسْتَضْعَفُونَ مَشَارِقَ الْأَرْضِ وَمَغَارِبَهَا الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ الْحُسْنَى عَلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا وَدَمَّرْنَا مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ وَقَوْمُهُ وَمَا كَانُوا يَعْرِشُونَ) (١٣٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَوْرَثْنَا): it takes two objects. The first is «الْقَوْمَ», and «الَّذِينَ كَانُوا» is a naʿt (adjective). On the second object there are three views. The first of them: (مَشَارِقَ الْأَرْضِ وَمَغَارِبَهَا), meaning the land of Syria (al-Shām) or Egypt. On this view there are two views on (الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا). One of them: it is a naʿt of the easts and wests. The second: it is a naʿt of الْأَرْض, and there is weakness in this, because it involves conjoining to the thing described before its adjective. The second opinion: the second object of أَوْرَثْنَا is «الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا», i.e. "the land that We blessed". On this view there are two views on the easts and wests. One of them: it is an adverb (ẓarf) of يُسْتَضْعَفُونَ. The second: its implied form is "they were deemed weak in the easts of the land and its wests"; when the preposition was dropped, the verb reached it directly, so it became accusative.
The third opinion:
الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا is a naʿt as preceded, and the second object is omitted, its implied form being "the land" or "the kingship". (مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ): «مَا» is in the sense of الَّذِي. On the noun of كَانَ there are two views. One of them: it is a pronoun referring to «مَا», and its khabar (predicate) is يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ, the resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) being omitted, i.e. يَصْنَعُهُ ("he made it").
The second: the noun of كَانَ is «فِرْعَوْنُ», and in يَصْنَعُ there is an agent pronoun. This is weak, because يَصْنَعُ is fit to govern فِرْعَوْن, so its postponement is not to be supposed, just as the postponement of the verb is not supposed in your saying قَامَ زَيْدٌ.
It is also said: «مَا» is maṣdariyya (infinitival) and «كَانَ» is redundant (zāʾida). It is also said: it is not redundant, but the incomplete (nāqiṣa) «كَانَ» does not separate between «مَا» and its ṣila; we have mentioned that at His saying (بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ). On this opinion «كَانَ» needs a noun, and it is weak for its noun to be the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), because the clause after it is the ṣila of «مَا», so it is not fit to explain [that pronoun], and the clarification and completion of the noun are not achieved by it, because what is explained must be future [Translator's note: so printed («مُسْتَقْبَلًا»); perhaps «مُسْتَقِلًّا», "independent", is meant.]. So the need arises for us to make فِرْعَوْن the noun of كَانَ, with a pronoun in «يَصْنَعُ» referring back to him. And (يَعْرِشُونَ): with ḍamma and with kasra on the rāʾ, two dialect forms; and likewise (يَعْكُفُونَ); both have been read in both [words].

ukberi-tibyan:138-138.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَاوَزْنَا بِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ الْبَحْرَ فَأَتَوْا عَلَى قَوْمٍ يَعْكُفُونَ عَلَى أَصْنَامٍ لَهُمْ قَالُوا يَا مُوسَى اجْعَلْ لَنَا إِلَهًا كَمَا لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ) (١٣٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَجَاوَزْنَا بِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ الْبَحْرَ): the bāʾ here is transitivising, like the hamza and the shadda, i.e. "We made the Children of Israel cross the sea" (أَجَزْنَا / جَوَّزْنَا).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَمَا لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ): on «مَا» there are three views. The first of them: it is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the clause after it is its ṣila; what makes this acceptable is that the adverbial phrase is understood as [standing for] a verb.
The second: «مَا» is in the sense of الَّذِي, the resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) being omitted, and آلِهَةٌ is a badal (substitute) from it, its implied form being "like that which is theirs"; and the kāf with what it governs is a naʿt (adjective) of إِلَهًا, i.e. "a god resembling that which they have". The third view: «مَا» restrains (kāffa) the kāf, since the rule of the kāf is that it enters on a single word; so when its entering on a clause was intended, it was restrained by مَا.

ukberi-tibyan:139-139.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ مُتَبَّرٌ مَا هُمْ فِيهِ وَبَاطِلٌ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) (١٣٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا هُمْ فِيهِ): «مَا» may be nominative by مُتَبَّرٌ, because it is strengthened by occurring as a khabar (predicate); and «مَا» may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with مُتَبَّرٌ a fronted khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (المص (1) كِتَابٌ أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ فَلَا يَكُنْ فِي صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ مِنْهُ لِتُنْذِرَ بِهِ وَذِكْرَى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ) (2).
(المص): we have mentioned at the beginning of al-Baqara what may apply here. It is possible that these letters are in the position of a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «كِتَابٌ» its khabar (predicate); or that they are the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "what is called by it is «المص»," with كِتَابٌ being the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this" or "it." (أُنْزِلَ): an adjective of it.
(فَلَا يَكُنْ): the prohibition is in wording directed at the حَرَج ("constriction"), and in meaning at the one addressed, i.e. "do not feel constricted by it."
(مِنْهُ): a naʿt (adjective) of الْحَرَج, and it is for the beginning of the extent, i.e. "do not feel constricted because of it."
(لِتُنْذِرَ): the lām may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) أُنْزِلَ, or to His saying فَلَا يَكُنْ, i.e. "do not feel constricted by it, so that you may be able [to convey] the revelation"; thus the hāʾ in مِنْهُ refers to the Book or to the sending down, and the hāʾ in «بِهِ» refers to the Book. (وَذِكْرَى): there are three views on it.
The first: it is accusative, and on that there are two views. One: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in أُنْزِلَ, what lies between them being parenthetical. The other: that it is conjoined to the position of لِتُنْذِرَ, [i.e.] "and to remind," i.e. "and as a reminder (وَلِذِكْرَى)." The second: that it is in the position of the nominative, and on that there are two views. One: it is conjoined to كِتَاب. The other: the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and it is a reminder."
The third view: that it is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the position of تُنْذِرَ. Some permitted conjoining it to the hāʾ in «بِهِ»; this is weak, because the preposition was not repeated.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (اتَّبِعُوا مَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ قَلِيلًا مَا تَذَكَّرُونَ) (3).
His saying (مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): it may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) أُنْزِلَ and be for the beginning of the extent; or be attached to an omitted word and be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "sent down to you, coming from your Lord." (مِنْ دُونِهِ): a ḥāl of أَوْلِيَاء. (قَلِيلًا مَا تَذَكَّرُونَ): like (فَقَلِيلًا مَا يُؤْمِنُونَ), which has been discussed in al-Baqara.
«تَذَكَّرُونَ» is read undoubled (تَذَكَّرُونَ), with the omission of one of the two tāʾs, and doubled (تَذَّكَّرُونَ), with assimilation.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَكَمْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا فَجَاءَهَا بَأْسُنَا بَيَاتًا أَوْ هُمْ قَائِلُونَ) (4).
His saying (وَكَمْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ): regarding «كَمْ» there are two views. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ» is an explanation, مِنْ being redundant (zāʾida); and the khabar (predicate) is «أَهْلَكْنَاهَا». The feminine form of the pronoun returning to «كَمْ» is permitted because كَمْ means "towns" (قُرًى). Some mentioned that أَهْلَكْنَاهَا is an adjective of قَرْيَة and the khabar is «فَجَاءَهَا بَأْسُنَا»; this is an oversight, because the fāʾ prevents that.
The second: that «كَمْ» is in the position of the accusative by an omitted verb indicated by أَهْلَكْنَاهَا, the implied form being: "many of the towns We destroyed." The verb may not be placed before «كَمْ», even though it is declarative (khabariyya), because it takes the head of the sentence, since it resembles رُبَّ. The meaning is: "how many a town We intended to destroy," like His saying (فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ الْقُرْآنَ), i.e. "when you intend to recite it."
Some said it is a case of inversion (qalb), i.e. "how many a town Our punishment came to, so We destroyed it." Inversion is not needed here, so it would remain a mere case of [poetic] necessity. The implied form is: "We destroyed its people, and [Our punishment] came to its people." (بَيَاتًا): الْبَيَات is a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar, verbal noun), and it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). It may also be a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or it may have the status of an adverbial. (أَوْ هُمْ قَائِلُونَ): the clause is a ḥāl, and «أَوْ» is for detailing the clauses, i.e. Our punishment came to some of them by night and to some of them by day. The wāw here is the wāw of «أَوْ»; it is not the conjunction made quiescent for lightening. We have mentioned that at His saying (أَوَكُلَّمَا عَاهَدُوا عَهْدًا).

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَمَا كَانَ دَعْوَاهُمْ إِذْ جَاءَهُمْ بَأْسُنَا إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ) (5).
His saying (دَعْوَاهُمْ): it may be the noun (ism) of كَانَ, with (إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوا) the khabar (predicate); the reverse is also permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَنَقُصَّنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ بِعِلْمٍ وَمَا كُنَّا غَائِبِينَ) (7).
His saying (بِعِلْمٍ): it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "knowing."

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالْوَزْنُ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْحَقُّ فَمَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ) (8).
His saying (وَالْوَزْنُ): there are two views on it. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (يَوْمَئِذٍ) is its khabar (predicate), what governs the adverb being omitted, i.e. "and the weighing is taking place on that day." (الْحَقُّ): an adjective of الْوَزْن, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. The second: that الْوَزْن is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this is the weighing," and يَوْمَئِذٍ is an adverbial. On this view الْحَقُّ may not be an adjective, lest the relative be separated from its ṣila (relative clause).

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ فَأُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا يَظْلِمُونَ) (9).
His saying (بِمَا كَانُوا): «مَا» is maṣdariyya, i.e. "because of their wrongdoing," and the bāʾ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) خَسِرُوا.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: {وَلَقَد مكناكم فِي الأَرْض وَجَعَلنَا لكم فِيهَا معايش قَلِيلا مَا تشكرون}
His saying (مَعَايِشَ): the correct view is that the yāʾ is not given a hamza here, because it is a root letter. It was given a vowel because it is vowelled in origin; its pattern is مَعْيِشَة, like مَحْبِسَة. Some permitted that its original vowel was fatḥa (مَعْيَشَة) and that it underwent change by being made quiescent in the singular, just as it was changed in يَعِيشُ. Some gave it a hamza (مَعَائِش); this is very far-fetched, and its rationale is that the root letter was likened to the extra one, as in سَفِينَة and سَفَائِن. (قَلِيلًا مَا تَشْكُرُونَ): like what preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ لَمْ يَكُنْ مِنَ السَّاجِدِينَ) (11).
His saying (وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ): i.e. "you [yourselves]." It has also been said: the kāf is for the genus being addressed. There are many places here which have preceded. (لَمْ يَكُنْ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ إِذْ أَمَرْتُكَ قَالَ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِي مِنْ نَارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِنْ طِينٍ) (12).
His saying (أَلَّا): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (إِذْ): an adverbial of تَسْجُدَ.
His saying (خَلَقْتَنِي مِنْ نَارٍ): the preposition phrase is in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "You created me, being of fire." It may also be for the beginning of the extent, and so be attached to (mutaʿalliq) خَلَقْتَنِي. And لَا is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "what prevented you from prostrating?" «[Translator's note: the last sentence, about لَا in أَلَّا being redundant, belongs to the discussion of أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ; it stands at the end of the entry in the source.]»

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ فَاهْبِطْ مِنْهَا فَمَا يَكُونُ لَكَ أَنْ تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيهَا فَاخْرُجْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ الصَّاغِرِينَ) (13).
His saying (فِيهَا): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it may be an adverbial.

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ فَبِمَا أَغْوَيْتَنِي لَأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَاطَكَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ) (16).
His saying (فَبِمَا): the bāʾ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (لَأَقْعُدَنَّ). It has also been said that the bāʾ has the meaning of the lām. (صِرَاطَكَ): an adverbial. It has also been said that the implied form is: "on (عَلَى) Your path."

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ثُمَّ لَآتِيَنَّهُمْ مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ وَعَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ وَعَنْ شَمَائِلِهِمْ وَلَا تَجِدُ أَكْثَرَهُمْ شَاكِرِينَ) (17).
His saying (وَعَنْ شَمَائِلِهِمْ): it is the plural of شِمَال ("left side"); had it been pluralized as أَشْمِلَة and شُمُل, that would have been permissible. «[Translator's note: the printed text has «أَشِمْلَةً وَشَمْلَاءَ».]»

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ اخْرُجْ مِنْهَا مَذْءُومًا مَدْحُورًا لَمَنْ تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنْكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ) (18).
His saying (مَذْءُومًا): it is read with hamza, and it is from ذَأَمْتُهُ, when I find fault with him. It is also read «مَذُومًا», with wāw and without hamza, and there are two views on it. The first: that the vowel of the hamza was cast onto the dhāl and the hamza dropped. The second: that its original is مَذِيم, because its verb is ذَامَهُ يَذِيمُهُ ذَيْمًا; the yāʾ was changed into wāw, as they said مَكُول for مَكِيل and مَشُوب for مَشِيب. It and what follows it are two ḥāls (circumstantials); it is also possible that «مَدْحُورًا» is a ḥāl of the pronoun in «مَذْءُومًا». (لَمَنْ): in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the implied oath together with its answer stands in place of the khabar (predicate), namely His saying (لَأَمْلَأَنَّ).
(مِنْكُمْ): an address to a group, although only an address to one person preceded; but He treated him as a group because he is their chief, or because it turns from the third person to direct address; the meaning is the same.

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَا آدَمُ اسْكُنْ أَنْتَ وَزَوْجُكَ الْجَنَّةَ فَكُلَا مِنْ حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ) (19).
His saying (هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةَ): it is read هَذِي without hāʾ. The origin of «ذَا» is ذَيّ, because of their saying ذَيَّا in the diminutive; the second yāʾ was dropped for lightness, and the first yāʾ was turned into alif, lest it remain like كَيْ. When you address [i.e. refer to] the feminine, the yāʾ is restored and the dhāl given kasra, so that the feminine and the change [to alif] do not combine on it. As for the hāʾ, it was made a compensation for what was dropped when it was restored to the original, and it was joined to a yāʾ [in pronunciation] because it resembles the pronoun hāʾ in form.

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا الشَّيْطَانُ لِيُبْدِيَ لَهُمَا مَا وُورِيَ عَنْهُمَا مِنْ سَوْآتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَاكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ الْخَالِدِينَ) (20).
His saying (مِنْ سَوْآتِهِمَا): the majority pronounce the hamza fully. It is also read with a wāw bearing fatḥa and the hamza dropped (سَوَاتِهِمَا); its rationale is that the vowel of the hamza was cast onto the wāw. It is also read with the wāw doubled and without hamza (سَوَّاتِهِمَا), by changing the hamza into wāw. It is also read «سَوْأَتُهُمَا», in the singular, it being a generic noun. (إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَا): i.e. "except for fear that you become," so it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). (مَلَكَيْنِ): with fatḥa on the lām and with kasra (مَلِكَيْنِ, "two kings"); the meaning is clear.

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَاسَمَهُمَا إِنِّي لَكُمَا لَمِنَ النَّاصِحِينَ) (21).
His saying (لَكُمَا لَمِنَ النَّاصِحِينَ): it is like His saying (وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ), which has been discussed in al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَدَلَّاهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا الشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْآتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِنْ وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ وَنَادَاهُمَا رَبُّهُمَا أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَنْ تِلْكُمَا الشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُلْ لَكُمَا إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ) (22).
His saying (فَدَلَّاهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ): the alif is a substitute for a yāʾ which is itself a substitute for a lām; the original is دَلَّلَهُمَا, from الدَّلَالَة ("guiding"), not from الدَّلَال ("coquetry"). Changing the lām was permissible because the word came to have three lāms.
(بِغُرُورٍ): the bāʾ may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) this verb, and it may be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the accusative pronoun, i.e. "while they were deceived."
His saying (وَطَفِقَا): it has the status of كَادَ, and its meaning is beginning to do the action.
(يَخْصِفَانِ): its past is خَصَفَ, and it is transitive to one object; the implied form is: "something «مِنْ وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ» (of the leaves of the Garden)."
It has been read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ṣād, undoubled (يُخْصِفَانِ); its past is أَخْصَفَ, and with the hamza it is transitive to two [objects], the implied form being: "they cover themselves."
It is also read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ṣād doubled with kasra, together with fatḥa on the khāʾ, and with kasra on it together with fatḥa on the yāʾ and with kasra on it. The explanation of that has been mentioned at His saying (يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ).
(عَنْ تِلْكُمَا): we have mentioned the origin of «تِلْكَ». The pointing is to the tree, which is one, while those addressed are two; therefore the particle of address was put in the dual.

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ فِيهَا تَحْيَوْنَ وَفِيهَا تَمُوتُونَ وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ) (25).
His saying (وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ): the wāw in principle conjoins these verbs to one another, but they were separated by the adverbial, because it is the conjoining of a clause to a clause.
تُخْرَجُونَ is read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and with fatḥa (تَخْرُجُونَ); the meaning of both is clear.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا بَنِي آدَمَ قَدْ أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاسًا يُوَارِي سَوْآتِكُمْ وَرِيشًا وَلِبَاسُ التَّقْوَى ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ ذَلِكَ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ) (26).
His saying (وَرِيشًا): it is the plural of رِيشَة. It is also read رِيَاشًا, and there are two views on it. The first: it is a plural whose singular is رِيش, like رِيح and رِيَاح. The second: that it is a noun of plurality (ism jamʿ), like اللِّبَاس. (وَلِبَاسُ التَّقْوَى): it is read in the accusative (وَلِبَاسَ), conjoined to رِيشًا. If it is asked: how does clothing and plumage "come down"? It is answered: since plumage and clothing grow by means of rain, and rain comes down, what is the effect was treated as the cause. It is also read in the nominative, as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (ذَلِكَ): a mubtadaʾ, (خَيْرٌ) its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of لِبَاس. It is also possible that ذَلِكَ is a naʿt (adjective) of لِبَاسُ, i.e. "the mentioned and pointed-to," or a badal (substitute) of it, or a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), with خَيْرٌ the khabar. It has also been said: لِبَاسُ التَّقْوَى is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "and what covers your private parts is the garment of piety," or the reverse, i.e. "and the garment of piety is what covers your private parts." In the speech there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "and the garment of the people of piety." It has also been said that the meaning is: "and the garment of guarding (الِاتِّقَاء), by which one guards against being looked at," so then there is no omission.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا بَنِي آدَمَ لَا يَفْتِنَنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ كَمَا أَخْرَجَ أَبَوَيْكُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ يَنْزِعُ عَنْهُمَا لِبَاسَهُمَا لِيُرِيَهُمَا سَوْآتِهِمَا إِنَّهُ يَرَاكُمْ هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا تَرَوْنَهُمْ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا الشَّيَاطِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ لِلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ) (27).
His saying (لَا يَفْتِنَنَّكُمُ): the prohibition in wording is directed at Satan, and the meaning is: do not follow Satan, lest he tempt you. (كَمَا أَخْرَجَ): i.e. "a temptation like the temptation of your parents by expulsion." (يَنْزِعُ عَنْهُمَا): the clause is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) — if you wish, of the agent pronoun in أَخْرَجَ, and if you wish, of the two parents, because it contains two pronouns referring to them. يَنْزِعُ narrates something that has already happened, because the stripping of the garment from them was before the expulsion. If it is said: Satan did not strip the garment from them, it is answered: but he was the cause, so the expulsion and the stripping were attributed to him. (هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُ): هُوَ is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the agent pronoun, so that conjoining to it becomes good.

ukberi-tibyan:140-140.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْغِيكُمْ إِلَهًا وَهُوَ فَضَّلَكُمْ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ) (١٤٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ): there are two views on it. One of them: it is the object of أَبْغِيكُمْ, and the implied form is أَبْغِي لَكُمْ ("I seek for you"), the lām having been dropped; (إِلَهًا) is a tamyīz (specification). The second: «إِلَهًا» is the object of أَبْغِيكُمْ, and «غَيْرَ اللَّهِ» is a naʿt (adjective) placed before it, so it became a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَهُوَ فَضَّلَكُمْ): it may be a ḥāl, and it may be resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:142-142.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَوَاعَدْنَا مُوسَى ثَلَاثِينَ لَيْلَةً وَأَتْمَمْنَاهَا بِعَشْرٍ فَتَمَّ مِيقَاتُ رَبِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً وَقَالَ مُوسَى لِأَخِيهِ هَارُونَ اخْلُفْنِي فِي قَوْمِي وَأَصْلِحْ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ الْمُفْسِدِينَ) (١٤٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ثَلَاثِينَ لَيْلَةً): it is a second object of وَاعَدْنَا, and in it there is the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being "the coming of thirty" or "the completion of thirty". And (أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً): a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being "so the appointed term [of his Lord] was completed, being full". It is also said: it is the object of تَمَّ, because its meaning is "reached", so it is like their saying بَلَغَتْ أَرْضُكَ جَرِيبَيْنِ ("your land reached two jarībs"). And (هَارُونَ): a badal (substitute) or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); had it been read in the nominative, it would have been a vocative, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).

ukberi-tibyan:143-143.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا جَاءَ مُوسَى لِمِيقَاتِنَا وَكَلَّمَهُ رَبُّهُ قَالَ رَبِّ أَرِنِي أَنْظُرْ إِلَيْكَ قَالَ لَنْ تَرَانِي وَلَكِنِ انْظُرْ إِلَى الْجَبَلِ فَإِنِ اسْتَقَرَّ مَكَانَهُ فَسَوْفَ تَرَانِي فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّى رَبُّهُ لِلْجَبَلِ جَعَلَهُ دَكًّا وَخَرَّ مُوسَى صَعِقًا فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَ قَالَ سُبْحَانَكَ تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) (١٤٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَعَلَهُ دَكًّا): i.e. "He made it", so it takes two objects. Whoever read «دَكًّا» made it a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of "the thing levelled"; it is also said its implied form is "possessing levelling". Whoever read it with the madd [دَكَّاءَ] made it like أَرْضٌ دَكَّاءُ ("flat land") or نَاقَةٌ دَكَّاءُ, which is the she-camel that has no hump. And (صَعِقًا): a concomitant ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:145-145.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَتَبْنَا لَهُ فِي الْأَلْوَاحِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَوْعِظَةً وَتَفْصِيلًا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ فَخُذْهَا بِقُوَّةٍ وَأْمُرْ قَوْمَكَ يَأْخُذُوا بِأَحْسَنِهَا سَأُرِيكُمْ دَارَ الْفَاسِقِينَ) (١٤٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَأُرِيكُمْ): in an irregular (shādhdh) reading it was read with a wāw after the hamza [سَأُورِيكُمْ]; it arises from lengthening (ishbāʿ), and it is far-fetched.

ukberi-tibyan:146-146.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَأَصْرِفُ عَنْ آيَاتِيَ الَّذِينَ يَتَكَبَّرُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ وَإِنْ يَرَوْا كُلَّ آيَةٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُوا بِهَا وَإِنْ يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ الرُّشْدِ لَا يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلًا وَإِنْ يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ الْغَيِّ يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلًا ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَكَانُوا عَنْهَا غَافِلِينَ) (١٤٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَبِيلَ الرُّشْدِ): it is read with ḍamma on the rāʾ and sukūn on the shīn, and with fatḥa on both [الرَّشَدِ], and «سَبِيلَ الرَّشَادِ» with the alif; and the meaning is the same.

ukberi-tibyan:147-147.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَلِقَاءِ الْآخِرَةِ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ هَلْ يُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) (١٤٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is «حَبِطَتْ». The khabar may also be «هَلْ يُجْزَوْنَ», with حَبِطَتْ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in كَذَّبُوا, قَدْ being intended.

ukberi-tibyan:148-148.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاتَّخَذَ قَوْمُ مُوسَى مِنْ بَعْدِهِ مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَهُ خُوَارٌ أَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّهُ لَا يُكَلِّمُهُمْ وَلَا يَهْدِيهِمْ سَبِيلًا اتَّخَذُوهُ وَكَانُوا ظَالِمِينَ) (١٤٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ): it is read with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, sukūn on the lām and the yāʾ without shadda [حَلْيِهِمْ], and it is a singular. It is also read with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, kasra on the lām and shadda on the yāʾ; it is a plural whose origin is حُلُوْيٌ [Translator's note: the printed text has «حُلُوَى».]; the wāw was changed into yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ, then the lām was given kasra to accord with it.
It is also read with kasra on the ḥāʾ and the lām and with shadda [حِلِيِّهِمْ], on the basis that the kasra was made to follow the kasra. (عِجْلًا): the object of اتَّخَذَ. And (جَسَدًا): a naʿt (adjective), a badal (substitute) or a bayān (explicative apposition). (مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ) may be a naʿt of عِجْلًا placed before it, so that it became a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to اتَّخَذَ, with the second object omitted, i.e. "as a god".

ukberi-tibyan:149-149.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا سُقِطَ فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ وَرَأَوْا أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ ضَلُّوا قَالُوا لَئِنْ لَمْ يَرْحَمْنَا رَبُّنَا وَيَغْفِرْ لَنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ) (١٤٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سُقِطَ فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun stand in the place of the fāʿil (agent) [i.e. as nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent], and the implied form is "remorse fell into their hands".

ukberi-tibyan:150-150.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ مُوسَى إِلَى قَوْمِهِ غَضْبَانَ أَسِفًا قَالَ بِئْسَمَا خَلَفْتُمُونِي مِنْ بَعْدِي أَعَجِلْتُمْ أَمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ وَأَلْقَى الْأَلْوَاحَ وَأَخَذَ بِرَأْسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُ إِلَيْهِ قَالَ ابْنَ أُمَّ إِنَّ الْقَوْمَ اسْتَضْعَفُونِي وَكَادُوا يَقْتُلُونَنِي فَلَا تُشْمِتْ بِيَ الْأَعْدَاءَ وَلَا تَجْعَلْنِي مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ) (١٥٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (غَضْبَانَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from مُوسَى. And (أَسِفًا): another ḥāl, a badal (substitute) from the one before it.
It may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun that is in غَضْبَانَ.
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَجُرُّهُ إِلَيْهِ): it may be a ḥāl from مُوسَى, and it may be a ḥāl from the head; it is weak for it to be a ḥāl from his brother. (قَالَ ابْنَ أُمَّ): it is read with kasra on the mīm, the kasra indicating the omitted yāʾ; and with fatḥa on it, and on this there are two views.
One of them: the alif has been dropped, the origin of the alif being the yāʾ; the mīm before it was given fatḥa, so it turned into an alif, and the fatḥa remained to indicate it, as they said يَا بِنْتَ عَمَّا. The second view: he made ابْن and الْأُمّ like خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ ("fifteen"), and made them both indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa.
(فَلَا تُشْمِتْ): the majority read ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the mīm, and (الْأَعْدَاءَ) is its object. It was also read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the mīm, with الْأَعْدَاءُ as its agent; the prohibition is in wording directed at the enemies and in meaning at someone else, namely Mūsā, as you say لَا أَرَيْنَكَ هَاهُنَا ("let me not see you here"). And it was read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the mīm and the accusative of الْأَعْدَاء; the implied form is "do not rejoice at my misfortune yourself, and so cause the enemies to rejoice at my misfortune", and the verb was dropped.

ukberi-tibyan:153-153.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ عَمِلُوا السَّيِّئَاتِ ثُمَّ تَابُوا مِنْ بَعْدِهَا وَآمَنُوا إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِهَا لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) (١٣٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ عَمِلُوا السَّيِّئَاتِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is «إِنَّ رَبَّكَ بَعْدَهَا لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ», the resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) being omitted, i.e. "forgiving to them" or "merciful to them".

ukberi-tibyan:154-154.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا سَكَتَ عَنْ مُوسَى الْغَضَبُ أَخَذَ الْأَلْوَاحَ وَفِي نُسْخَتِهَا هُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ) (١٥٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَفِي نُسْخَتِهَا هُدًى): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْأَلْوَاح.
(لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ): on the lām there are three views. The first of them: it is in the sense of "for the sake of their Lord",
so on this view the object of يَرْهَبُونَ is omitted, i.e. "they fear His punishment". The second: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, its implied form being "and those who humble themselves before their Lord". The third: it is redundant (zāʾida); and this became acceptable since the verb comes later.

ukberi-tibyan:155-155.t:
