Allah the Exalted said: (وَاخْتَارَ مُوسَى قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلًا لِمِيقَاتِنَا فَلَمَّا أَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ قَالَ رَبِّ لَوْ شِئْتَ أَهْلَكْتَهُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَإِيَّايَ أَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ السُّفَهَاءُ مِنَّا إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا فِتْنَتُكَ تُضِلُّ بِهَا مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتَهْدِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ أَنْتَ وَلِيُّنَا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْغَافِرِينَ) (١٥٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاخْتَارَ مُوسَى قَوْمَهُ): choosing takes two objects, one of them by means of a preposition, which has been dropped here; the implied form is "from his people". According to most, «سَبْعِينَ» may not be a badal (substitute), because what is substituted for is as if discarded, while choosing must have a thing chosen and a thing chosen from, and the badal would drop the thing chosen from. But I hold that the badal is permissible, though weak, the implied form being «seventy men of them». (أَتُهْلِكُنَا): it is said: it is a question, i.e. "will You include us all in the destruction?". It is also said: its meaning is negation, i.e. "You do not destroy one who has not sinned". And (مِنَّا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السُّفَهَاء. (تُضِلُّ بِهَا): it may be resumptive, and it may be a ḥāl from the kāf in فِتْنَتُكَ [Translator's note: so printed; the sense seems to require "it may not be a ḥāl", given the reason that follows.], since there is nothing here fit to govern the ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:156-156.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاكْتُبْ لَنَا فِي هَذِهِ الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ إِنَّا هُدْنَا إِلَيْكَ قَالَ عَذَابِي أُصِيبُ بِهِ مَنْ أَشَاءُ وَرَحْمَتِي وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَسَأَكْتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَاةَ وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِآيَاتِنَا يُؤْمِنُونَ) (١٥٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هُدْنَا): the well-known reading is ḍamma on the hāʾ, from هَادَ يَهُودُ when he repents. It was also read with kasra on it [هِدْنَا], from هَادَ يَهِيدُ when it moves or moves something, i.e. "we have moved our souls towards You". (مَنْ أَشَاءُ): the well-known [Translator's note: the printed text has the misprint «الْمَهْشُورُ» for «الْمَشْهُورُ».] reading has the shīn; it was also read with the sīn and fatḥa [أَسَاءَ], and it is then a past verb, i.e. "I punish the evildoer".

ukberi-tibyan:157-157.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الرَّسُولَ النَّبِيَّ الْأُمِّيَّ الَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُ مَكْتُوبًا عِنْدَهُمْ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ وَالْإِنْجِيلِ يَأْمُرُهُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَاهُمْ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْخَبَائِثَ وَيَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ وَالْأَغْلَالَ الَّتِي كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِهِ وَعَزَّرُوهُ وَنَصَرُوهُ وَاتَّبَعُوا النُّورَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مَعَهُ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ) (١٥٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ): on الَّذِينَ there are three views. The first of them: it is genitive, as
a naʿt (adjective) of لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ, or a badal (substitute) from it. The second: accusative, by implying أَعْنِي ("I mean"). The third: nominative, i.e. "they are those who follow". It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) being «يَأْمُرُهُمْ» [or] وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ.
(الْأُمِّيَّ): the well-known reading is ḍamma on the hamza, and it is a relational adjective (nisba) from الْأُمّ ("the mother"); it has been mentioned in al-Baqara. It was also read with fatḥa on it [الْأَمِّيَّ], and there are two views on this. One of them: it is a case of altering the nisba, as they said أَمَوِيٌّ [Translator's note: printed «أُمَوِيٌّ»; the point is the fatḥa variant أَمَوِيٌّ of the nisba to Umayya.]. The second: it is a nisba from الْأَمّ, which is the intended course, i.e. the one who is on the right course and rectitude.
(يَجِدُونَهُ): i.e. "they find his name". And (مَكْتُوبًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial). And (عِنْدَهُمْ): an adverb (ẓarf) of مَكْتُوبًا or of يَجِدُونَ. (يَأْمُرُهُمْ): it may be a khabar of الَّذِينَ, as has been mentioned; it may be resumptive; or it may be a ḥāl from النَّبِيّ, or from the pronoun in مَكْتُوبًا. (إِصْرَهُمْ): the majority read the singular, and it is a generic noun; it is also read «آصَارَهُمْ» in the plural, because of the different kinds of burden that were upon them, and for this reason He put الْأَغْلَال in the plural. (وَعَزَّرُوهُ): with shadda and without shadda; it has been mentioned in al-Māʾida.

ukberi-tibyan:158-158.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ جَمِيعًا الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ النَّبِيِّ الْأُمِّيِّ الَّذِي يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَكَلِمَاتِهِ وَاتَّبِعُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ) (١٥٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ): its position is accusative by implying أَعْنِي ("I mean"), i.e. [Translator's note: so printed («أَيْ»); «أَوْ», "or", is evidently meant.] in the position of a nominative by implying هُوَ. It is unlikely to be a naʿt (adjective) of اللَّه or a badal (substitute) from it, because of the separation between them by إِلَيْكُمْ and its ḥāl [جَمِيعًا], and it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to رَسُولُ.

ukberi-tibyan:160-160.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَطَّعْنَاهُمُ اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ أَسْبَاطًا أُمَمًا وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسَى إِذِ اسْتَسْقَاهُ قَوْمُهُ أَنِ اضْرِبْ بِعَصَاكَ الْحَجَرَ فَانْبَجَسَتْ مِنْهُ اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَشْرَبَهُمْ وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ الْغَمَامَ وَأَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَى كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَكِنْ كَانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ) (١٦٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَقَطَّعْنَاهُمُ اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ): there are two views on it. One of them: قَطَّعْنَا is in the sense of صَيَّرْنَا ("We made"), so اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ is a second object. The second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "We divided them into groups". And (عَشْرَةَ): with sukūn, kasra and fatḥa on the shīn are dialect forms, and it has been read with them. And (أَسْبَاطًا): a badal (substitute) from «اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ», not a tamyīz (specification), because it is a plural. And (أُمَمًا): a naʿt (adjective) of أَسْبَاطًا, or a badal after a badal. He made «اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ» feminine because the implied form is "twelve communities (أُمَّة)". (أَنِ اضْرِبْ): it may be maṣdariyya (infinitival), and it may be in the sense of أَيْ (explicative "that is").

ukberi-tibyan:161-161.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ قِيلَ لَهُمُ اسْكُنُوا هَذِهِ الْقَرْيَةَ وَكُلُوا مِنْهَا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمْ وَقُولُوا حِطَّةٌ وَادْخُلُوا الْبَابَ سُجَّدًا نَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطِيئَاتِكُمْ سَنَزِيدُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ) (١٦١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حِطَّةٌ): it is like the one in al-Baqara. And (نَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ): what indicates [the treatment of] what is here has been mentioned in al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:163-163.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاسْأَلْهُمْ عَنِ الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي كَانَتْ حَاضِرَةَ الْبَحْرِ إِذْ يَعْدُونَ فِي السَّبْتِ إِذْ تَأْتِيهِمْ حِيتَانُهُمْ يَوْمَ سَبْتِهِمْ شُرَّعًا وَيَوْمَ لَا يَسْبِتُونَ لَا تَأْتِيهِمْ كَذَلِكَ نَبْلُوهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ) (١٦٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَنِ الْقَرْيَةِ): i.e. about the news of the town; and this omitted element is what puts in the accusative the adverb (ẓarf), which is His saying إِذْ يَعْدُونَ. It is also said: it is an adverb of حَاضِرَةَ; what allows this is that the town existed at that time and was later ruined. يَعْدُونَ is without shadda; it is also read with shadda and fatḥa [يَعَدُّونَ], the origin being يَعْتَدُونَ; its parallel has been mentioned at «يَخْصِفُ». (إِذْ تَأْتِيهِمْ): an adverb of «يَعْدُونَ». And (حِيتَانُهُمْ): the plural of حُوتٌ ("fish"); the wāw was replaced by yāʾ because it is vowelless and what precedes it has kasra. (شُرَّعًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْحِيتَان. (وَيَوْمَ لَا يَسْبِتُونَ): an adverb of His saying «لَا تَأْتِيهِمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:164-164.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ قَالَتْ أُمَّةٌ مِنْهُمْ لِمَ تَعِظُونَ قَوْمًا اللَّهُ مُهْلِكُهُمْ أَوْ مُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا قَالُوا مَعْذِرَةً إِلَى رَبِّكُمْ وَلَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ) (١٦٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَعْذِرَةً): it is read in the nominative, i.e. "our admonition is an excuse"; and in the accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. "our admonishing is for the sake of excuse". It is also said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. mafʿūl muṭlaq], i.e. "we excuse ourselves an excusing".

ukberi-tibyan:165-165.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا نَسُوا مَا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ أَنْجَيْنَا الَّذِينَ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ السُّوءِ وَأَخَذْنَا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا بِعَذَابٍ بَئِيسٍ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ) (١٦٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِعَذَابٍ بَئِيسٍ): it is read with fatḥa on the bāʾ, kasra on the hamza and a vowelless yāʾ after it.
There are two views on it.
One of them: it is a naʿt (adjective) of the punishment, like شَدِيدٍ ("severe"). The second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like النَّذِيرُ, and the implied form is "with a punishment possessing بَأْس", i.e. possessing severity. It is also read the same way except with the hamza lightened and brought close to the yāʾ. It is also read with fatḥa on the bāʾ and a hamza with kasra with no yāʾ after it [بَئِسٍ]; on this there are two views. One of them: it is an adjective like قَلِقٌ and حَنِقٌ. The second: it is transferred from بِئْسَ, which is set up for blame, to [being] a description. It is also read the same way except with kasra on the bāʾ by assimilation (itbāʿ) [بِئِسٍ]. It is also read with kasra on the bāʾ and sukūn on the hamza [بِئْسٍ]; its origin is fatḥa on the bāʾ and kasra on the hamza, then he put kasra on the bāʾ by assimilation and made the hamza vowelless for lightness. It is also read the same way except that in place of the hamza there is a vowelless yāʾ [بِيسٍ], and that is a lightening, as you say ذِيبٌ for ذِئْبٌ. It is also read with fatḥa on the bāʾ and kasra on the yāʾ [بَيِسٍ], its origin being a hamza with kasra that was replaced by yāʾ. It is also read with two yāʾs on the pattern fayʿāl [Translator's note: so printed; the pattern meant is unclear.]. It is also read «بَيَسَ» with fatḥa on the bāʾ and the yāʾ without hamza; its origin is a vowelless bāʾ [Translator's note: so printed; "a vowelless yāʾ" is evidently meant.] and a hamza with fatḥa, except that the vowel of the hamza was thrown onto the yāʾ, and the yāʾ was not turned into an alif because its vowel is accidental. It is also read «بَيْأَسٌ», like ضَيْغَمٌ. It is also read with fatḥa on the bāʾ and kasra and shadda on the yāʾ [بَيِّسٍ], like سَيِّدٌ and مَيِّتٌ; this is weak, since there is nothing like it in the language among words with hamza. It is also read «بَأْيَسٌ» with fatḥa on the bāʾ, sukūn on the hamza and fatḥa on the yāʾ; this is far-fetched, since there is no faʿīl in the language [Translator's note: so printed; the pattern faʿyal is evidently meant.]. It is also read the same way except with kasra on the bāʾ, like عِثِيرٌ and حِدِيمٌ [Translator's note: so printed; the known forms are عِثْيَرٌ and حِذْيَمٌ, on the pattern fiʿyal.].

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ أَمَرَ رَبِّي بِالْقِسْطِ وَأَقِيمُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ وَادْعُوهُ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ كَمَا بَدَأَكُمْ تَعُودُونَ) (29) (فَرِيقًا هَدَى وَفَرِيقًا حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الضَّلَالَةُ إِنَّهُمُ اتَّخَذُوا الشَّيَاطِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ) (30).
His saying (وَأَقِيمُوا): regarding the implied structure of the speech there are two views. The first: it is conjoined to the position of «الْقِسْطِ» according to the meaning, i.e. "my Lord commanded, saying: act justly, and set …" The second: there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: "so turn [to Him] and set …" (الدِّينَ): accusative by مُخْلِصِينَ. Fatḥa on the lām in «مُخْلِصِينَ» (مُخْلَصِينَ) is not permissible here, because the mention of the object prevents the agent from being left unnamed (i.e. the passive). (كَمَا): the kāf is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "you will return, a returning like your beginning." (فَرِيقًا هَدَى): there are two views on it. The first: it is accusative by هَدَى, and the second «فَرِيقًا» is accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being: "and He sent astray a group," what follows being an explanation of the omitted [verb]. The whole of the speech is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «تَعُودُونَ», with «قَدْ» intended along with the verb, the implied form being: "you will return, He having guided a group and sent astray a group." The second view: that «فَرِيقًا» in both places is a ḥāl; «هَدَى» is a description of the first, and (حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ) is a description of the second; the implied form is: "you will return as two groups," and Ubayy read it so. The feminine tāʾ was not attached to «حَقَّ» because of the separation, or because the feminine is not real.

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا بَنِي آدَمَ خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا وَلَا تُسْرِفُوا إِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ) (31).
His saying (عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ): an adverbial of «خُذُوا», and not a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the adornment, because taking it happens before that. «[Translator's note: the printed text has «لِأَنَّ أَحَدَهَا», rendered here in the sense of «أَخْذَهَا» ("taking it").]» There is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: "upon heading for every mosque."

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ مَنْ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِ وَالطَّيِّبَاتِ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ قُلْ هِيَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا خَالِصَةً يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ كَذَلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ) (32).
His saying (قُلْ هِيَ): هِيَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and regarding the khabar (predicate) there are six views. The first: (خَالِصَةً), on the reading of those who read it in the nominative (خَالِصَةٌ); on this view the lām is attached to (mutaʿalliq) خَالِصَة, i.e. "it is exclusive to whoever believed in this world," and «يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ» is an adverbial of خَالِصَة. Attaching the two adverbials to it is not prevented, because the lām is for clarification (tabyīn). «[Translator's note: the printed text continues «وَ (يَوْم) لَا: ظَرْفٌ مَحْضٌ», which appears garbled; it is rendered as: "and يَوْم is a pure adverbial."]» And فِي is attached to آمَنُوا.
The second: that the khabar is لِلَّذِينَ, خَالِصَة is a second khabar, and فِي is attached to آمَنُوا. The third: that the khabar is لِلَّذِينَ, and فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا is governed by the adverbial phrase, namely the lām, i.e. "it is established for those who believed in the life of this world," with خَالِصَة a second khabar.
The fourth: that the khabar is فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا, and لِلَّذِينَ is attached to «خَالِصَةٌ». The fifth: that the lām [phrase] is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the adverbial phrase after it, according to the view of al-Akhfash. The sixth: that «خَالِصَةً» is accusative as a ḥāl, on the reading of those who read it in the accusative; what governs it is لِلَّذِينَ, or فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا if you make it a khabar or a ḥāl. The implied meaning is: "it belongs to those who believed, in the life of this world, being exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection," i.e. they share in the adornment in this world, and it will be exclusively theirs in the Hereafter. It is not permissible for زِينَةُ اللَّهِ to govern «خَالِصَةً», because He described it with His saying الَّتِي, and a maṣdar (verbal noun), when qualified, does not govern; nor His saying «أَخْرَجَ», because of the separation between them, namely His saying قُلْ. Abū ʿAlī permitted «حَرَّمَ» to govern it; that is far-fetched, also because of the separation. (كَذَلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ): we have mentioned the i'rab of its like in al-Baqara and al-Anʿām.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ رَبِّيَ الْفَوَاحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ وَالْإِثْمَ وَالْبَغْيَ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ وَأَنْ تُشْرِكُوا بِاللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطَانًا وَأَنْ تَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ) (33).
His saying (مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ): two badals (substitutes) of الْفَوَاحِش. (بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ): attached to (mutaʿalliq) الْبَغْي. It has also been said: it is [a ḥāl] of the pronoun contained in the maṣdar (verbal noun), since the implied form is: "and that you transgress without right." According to these, the maṣdar contains a pronoun. «[Translator's note: the printed text has «وَإِنْ تَبْغُوا»; the sense is «وَأَنْ تَبْغُوا».]»

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلٌ فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لَا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ سَاعَةً وَلَا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ) (34).
His saying (جَاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ): it is a singular in the place of a plural. Ibn Sīrīn read آجَالُهُمْ, according to the base meaning, because each one of them has a term.

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا بَنِي آدَمَ إِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِي فَمَنِ اتَّقَى وَأَصْلَحَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ) (35).
His saying (يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ): it may be in the position of the nominative as an adjective of رُسُل; or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of رُسُل, or of the pronoun in the adverbial phrase.

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِآيَاتِهِ أُولَئِكَ يَنَالُهُمْ نَصِيبُهُمْ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنَا يَتَوَفَّوْنَهُمْ قَالُوا أَيْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ قَالُوا ضَلُّوا عَنَّا وَشَهِدُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا كَافِرِينَ) (37).
His saying (مِنَ الْكِتَابِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (نَصِيبُهُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ ادْخُلُوا فِي أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ فِي النَّارِ كُلَّمَا دَخَلَتْ أُمَّةٌ لَعَنَتْ أُخْتَهَا حَتَّى إِذَا ادَّارَكُوا فِيهَا جَمِيعًا قَالَتْ أُخْرَاهُمْ لِأُولَاهُمْ رَبَّنَا هَؤُلَاءِ أَضَلُّونَا فَآتِهِمْ عَذَابًا ضِعْفًا مِنَ النَّارِ قَالَ لِكُلٍّ ضِعْفٌ وَلَكِنْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ) (38).
His saying (مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ): it may be an adverbial of «خَلَتْ», or an adjective of أُمَم. (مِنَ الْجِنِّ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in خَلَتْ, or another adjective of أُمَم. (فِي النَّارِ): attached to (mutaʿalliq) ادْخُلُوا; it may also be an adjective of أُمَم, or an adverbial of خَلَتْ. (ادَّارَكُوا): it is read with the dāl doubled and an alif after it. Its origin is تَدَارَكُوا; the tāʾ was changed into dāl and made quiescent so that its assimilation would be valid, then the connecting hamza was brought in for it, so that pronouncing the quiescent letter would be possible. It is also read in the same way but without an alif after the dāl (ادَّرَكُوا); on this its pattern is افْتَعَلُوا, the tāʾ here being after the dāl, like اقْتَتَلُوا. In the irregular (shādhdh) readings it has been read «تَدَارَكُوا», according to the base form, i.e. "they overtook one another." It has also been read «إِذَا إِدَّارَكُوا», with the hamza cut off from what precedes it and given kasra, with the intention of pausing on what precedes it and beginning with it.
It has also been read «إِذَا ادَّارَكُوا» with a single quiescent alif followed by the doubled dāl; this combines two quiescent letters, which was permitted because the second is assimilated, as they said دَابَّة and شَابَّة. It was permitted across separate words just as it is permitted within one word. Some have said «اثْنَا عَشْرَ» with the alif retained and the ʿayn quiescent; you will see it in its place, if Allah the Exalted wills. (جَمِيعًا): a ḥāl. (ضِعْفًا): an adjective of عَذَاب, in the sense of مُضَعَّف or مُضَاعَف ("doubled"). (مِنَ النَّارِ): another adjective; it may also be a ḥāl.
His saying (لِكُلٍّ ضِعْفٌ): i.e. "for each there is a doubled punishment of the Fire"; it was omitted because the first indicates it. (وَلَكِنْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ): with tāʾ, as direct address, and with yāʾ (يَعْلَمُونَ), as the third person.

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا عَنْهَا لَا تُفَتَّحُ لَهُمْ أَبْوَابُ السَّمَاءِ وَلَا يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ حَتَّى يَلِجَ الْجَمَلُ فِي سَمِّ الْخِيَاطِ وَكَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُجْرِمِينَ) (40).
His saying (لَا تُفَتَّحُ): it is read with tāʾ; in the second tāʾ, both undoubled (تُفْتَحُ) and doubled, for multiplicity, are permissible.
It is also read with yāʾ (يُفَتَّحُ), because the feminine of الْأَبْوَاب is not real, and also because of the separation. (الْجَمَلُ): it is read with fatḥa on the jīm, and it is the well-known camel.
In the irregular (shādhdh) readings it is read with the mīm quiescent (الْجَمْلُ); the better view is that this is a dialectal variant, because lightening a fatḥa-vowelled letter is weak. It is also read with ḍamma on the jīm and fatḥa on the mīm, doubled (الْجُمَّلُ), and it is the thick rope; it is a plural like صَوْم and قَوْم «[Translator's note: so vocalized in the source; the pattern intended is presumably صُوَّم and قُوَّم.]». It is also read with ḍamma on the jīm and the mīm, undoubled (الْجُمُلُ), and it is a plural like أَسَد and أُسُد. It is also read in the same way except that the mīm is quiescent (الْجُمْلُ), which is by lightening of the ḍamma-vowelled letter. (سَمِّ الْخِيَاطِ): fatḥa and ḍamma on the sīn are two dialectal variants. (وَكَذَلِكَ): in the position of the accusative by «نَجْزِي», as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَهُمْ مِنْ جَهَنَّمَ مِهَادٌ وَمِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ غَوَاشٍ وَكَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ) (41).
His saying (غَوَاشٍ): it is the plural of غَاشِيَة ("covering"). Regarding the tanwīn here there are three views. The first: that it is the tanwīn of full declension (ṣarf); that is because they dropped the yāʾ from «غَوَاشِي», so its form fell short of the form of مَسَاجِد and became like سَلَام; therefore it was fully declined. The second: that it is a compensation for the omitted yāʾ.
The third: that it is a compensation for the vowel due to the yāʾ; when the vowel was dropped and compensated for by the tanwīn, the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
On this question there is a long discussion for which this book has no room.

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ) (42).
His saying (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and regarding the khabar (predicate) there are two views. The first: «لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا», the implied form being "of them," so the returning pronoun was omitted, as it was omitted in His saying (وَلَمَنْ صَبَرَ وَغَفَرَ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمِنْ عَزْمِ الْأُمُورِ).
The second: that the khabar is «أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ», and «لَا نُكَلِّفُ» is parenthetical between them.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِمْ مِنْ غِلٍّ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمُ الْأَنْهَارُ وَقَالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي هَدَانَا لِهَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لِنَهْتَدِيَ لَوْلَا أَنْ هَدَانَا اللَّهُ لَقَدْ جَاءَتْ رُسُلُ رَبِّنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَنُودُوا أَنْ تِلْكُمُ الْجَنَّةُ أُورِثْتُمُوهَا بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) (43).
His saying (مِنْ غِلٍّ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «مَا». (تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمُ): the clause is in the position of a ḥāl of the pronoun in the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), and what governs it is the meaning of the annexation.
His saying (هَدَانَا لِهَذَا): we have mentioned it in al-Fātiḥa. (وَمَا كُنَّا): the wāw is circumstantial (wāw al-ḥāl), and it may be resumptive. It is also read without the wāw (مَا كُنَّا), as a resumptive (new) sentence. (لِنَهْتَدِيَ): we have mentioned the i'rab of its like at His saying (مَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ). (أَنْ هَدَانَا): the two together are interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar), and its position is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), because the noun occurring after this «لَوْلَا» is so. The answer of لَوْلَا is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, its implied form being: "had Allah not guided us, we would not have been guided." For this reason the reading with the wāw omitted is good. (أَنْ تِلْكُمُ): regarding «أَنْ» there are two views. The first: it means أَيْ ("that is"), has no grammatical position, and is an explanation of the calling. The second: that it is lightened from the heavy form (أَنَّ); its noun is omitted and the clause after it is its khabar (predicate), i.e. "and they were called: that it is: this is the Garden," the hāʾ being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). The position of the whole speech is accusative by نُودُوا, or genitive on the implied form "with (بِ) that it is." (أُورِثْتُمُوهَا): it is read with the letters pronounced distinctly, according to the base, and with assimilation [of the thāʾ into the tāʾ], because the tāʾ shares with it the quality of whispering (hams) and is close to it in point of articulation. The position of the clause is accusative as a ḥāl of الْجَنَّة, and what governs it is the sense of pointing in تِلْكَ. It is not permissible for it to be a ḥāl of تِلْكَ, for two reasons.
The first: that the khabar separates them. The second: that «تِلْكَ» is a mubtadaʾ, and the inceptive state (ibtidāʾ) does not govern a ḥāl. It is also possible that الْجَنَّة is a naʿt (adjective) of تِلْكُمْ, or a badal (substitute), with أُورِثْتُمُوهَا the khabar.
It is not permissible for the clause to be a ḥāl of the kāf and mīm, because the kāf is a particle of address, and the one a ḥāl describes cannot be a particle; and because the ḥāl comes after the speech is complete, and the speech is not complete with تِلْكُمْ.

ukberi-tibyan:167-167.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكَ لَيَبْعَثَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ مَنْ يَسُومُهُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَسَرِيعُ الْعِقَابِ وَإِنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) (١٦٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَأَذَّنَ): it is in the sense of أَذَّنَ, i.e. "He made known". (إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَأَذَّنَ or to «يَبْعَثَنَّ», and this is the more plausible; it is not attached to «يَسُومُهُمْ», because the ṣila or the naʿt (adjective) does not govern what precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:168-168.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَطَّعْنَاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أُمَمًا مِنْهُمُ الصَّالِحُونَ وَمِنْهُمْ دُونَ ذَلِكَ وَبَلَوْنَاهُمْ بِالْحَسَنَاتِ وَالسَّيِّئَاتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ) (١٦٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَقَطَّعْنَاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أُمَمًا): [أُمَمًا is] a second object, or a ḥāl (circumstantial). (مِنْهُمُ الصَّالِحُونَ): a naʿt (adjective) of أُمَمًا, or a badal (substitute) from it. And (دُونَ ذَلِكَ): an adverb (ẓarf), or a khabar (predicate), according to what we mentioned at His saying (لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:169-169.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَخَلَفَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ وَرِثُوا الْكِتَابَ يَأْخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هَذَا الْأَدْنَى وَيَقُولُونَ سَيُغْفَرُ لَنَا وَإِنْ يَأْتِهِمْ عَرَضٌ مِثْلُهُ يَأْخُذُوهُ أَلَمْ يُؤْخَذْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِيثَاقُ الْكِتَابِ أَنْ لَا يَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْحَقَّ وَدَرَسُوا مَا فِيهِ وَالدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ) (١٩٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَرِثُوا الْكِتَابَ): a naʿt (adjective) of خَلْفٌ. (يَأْخُذُونَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in وَرِثُوا. (وَدَرَسُوا): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «وَرِثُوا», and His saying «أَلَمْ يُؤْخَذْ» is parenthetical between them. It is also read ادَّارَسُوا, which is like ادَّارَكُوا فِيهَا, and it has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:170-170.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ يُمَسِّكُونَ بِالْكِتَابِ وَأَقَامُوا الصَّلَاةَ إِنَّا لَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُصْلِحِينَ) (١٩٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ يُمَسِّكُونَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (إِنَّا لَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُصْلِحِينَ), the implied form being "among them". Or, if you wish, you may say: He put the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, i.e. "We do not let their reward be lost". Or, if you wish, you may say: since الْمُصْلِحُونَ is a genus and the mubtadaʾ is one [part] of it, you could dispense with a pronoun. يُمَسِّكُونَ is with shadda, and its past is مَسَّكَ [Translator's note: printed «مَسَكَ».]; it is also read without shadda, from أَمْسَكَ. The meaning of both readings is "he held fast to the Book", i.e. acted upon it; and الْكِتَاب is a genus.

ukberi-tibyan:171-171.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ نَتَقْنَا الْجَبَلَ فَوْقَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُ ظُلَّةٌ وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُ وَاقِعٌ بِهِمْ خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُمْ بِقُوَّةٍ وَاذْكُرُوا مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ) (١٧١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ نَتَقْنَا): i.e. "and remember when…". And (فَوْقَهُمْ): an adverb (ẓarf) of نَتَقْنَا, or a non-emphatic ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْجَبَل, because raising the mountain above them specifies it to one of the directions of height. (كَأَنَّهُ): the clause is likewise a ḥāl from الْجَبَل. (وَظَنُّوا): resumptive. It may also be maʿṭūf (conjoined) to نَتَقْنَا, so that its position is genitive; and it may be a ḥāl, with قَدْ intended with it. (خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُمْ): it has been mentioned in al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:172-173.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى شَهِدْنَا أَنْ تَقُولُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَذَا غَافِلِينَ (١٧٢) أَوْ تَقُولُوا إِنَّمَا أَشْرَكَ آبَاؤُنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةً مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ أَفَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ) (١٧٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ أَخَذَ): i.e. "and remember". (مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ): a badal (substitute) from بَنِي آدَمَ, i.e. "from the backs of the children of Adam"; He repeated the preposition with the badal, and it is the badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). (أَنْ تَقُولُوا): with yāʾ and with tāʾ; it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. "for fear that you should say"; and likewise (أَوْ تَقُولُوا).

ukberi-tibyan:176-176.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَرَفَعْنَاهُ بِهَا وَلَكِنَّهُ أَخْلَدَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ الْكَلْبِ إِنْ تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْهِ يَلْهَثْ أَوْ تَتْرُكْهُ يَلْهَثْ ذَلِكَ مَثَلُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا فَاقْصُصِ الْقَصَصَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ) (١٧٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنْ تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْهِ يَلْهَثْ أَوْ تَتْرُكْهُ يَلْهَثْ): the whole utterance is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْكَلْب, its implied form being "he resembles the dog panting in every state".

ukberi-tibyan:177-177.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَاءَ مَثَلًا الْقَوْمُ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَأَنْفُسَهُمْ كَانُوا يَظْلِمُونَ) (١٧٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَاءَ): it is in the sense of بِئْسَ, and its fāʿil (agent) is implied, i.e. "evil is the example". And (مَثَلًا): the explainer [tamyīz] of «الْقَوْمُ», i.e. "the example of the people" [Translator's note: printed «مِثْلَ الْقَوْمِ»; the sense requires «مَثَلُ الْقَوْمِ», as the sequel shows.]; this implied form is necessary, because the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is of the same genus as the agent of بِئْسَ, and the agent is the example, while the people are not of the genus of the example. So the implied form must be "the example of the people"; He omitted it and put الْقَوْم in its place.

ukberi-tibyan:179-179.t:
قَالَ تَعَالَى {وَلَقَد ذرأنا لِجَهَنَّم كثيرا من الْجِنّ وَالْإِنْس لَهُم قُلُوب لَا يفقهُونَ بهَا}
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِجَهَنَّمَ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to ذَرَأْنَا, and it may be attached to an omitted element, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from كَثِيرًا, i.e. "many, for Hell". And (مِنَ الْجِنِّ): a naʿt (adjective) of كَثِيرًا. (لَهُمْ قُلُوبٌ): likewise a naʿt of كَثِيرًا.

ukberi-tibyan:180-180.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِلَّهِ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى فَادْعُوهُ بِهَا وَذَرُوا الَّذِينَ يُلْحِدُونَ فِي أَسْمَائِهِ سَيُجْزَوْنَ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) (١٨٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى): الْحُسْنَى is a singular adjective of a plural noun described, and it was made feminine because of the femininity of the plural. (يُلْحِدُونَ): it is read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ḥāʾ, its past being أَلْحَدَ; and with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ḥāʾ, its past being لَحَدَ; and they are two dialect forms.

ukberi-tibyan:181-181.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِمَّنْ خَلَقْنَا أُمَّةٌ يَهْدُونَ بِالْحَقِّ وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ) (١٨١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمِمَّنْ خَلَقْنَا): [مَنْ is] an indefinite noun described [by what follows], or in the sense of الَّذِي.

ukberi-tibyan:182-182.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ) (١٨٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ) is the khabar (predicate). It may also be in the position of an accusative by an omitted verb, which the one mentioned explains, i.e. "We shall draw on step by step those who…".

ukberi-tibyan:183-183.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ) (١٨٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأُمْلِي): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and I grant respite". It may also be maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «نَسْتَدْرِجُ», and it may be resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:184-184.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا مَا بِصَاحِبِهِمْ مِنْ جِنَّةٍ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ) (١٨٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا بِصَاحِبِهِمْ): on «مَا» there are two views. One of them: it is negating, and there is an ellipsis in the speech, its implied form being "have they not reflected on their saying: in him is madness?". The second: it is interrogative, i.e. "have they not reflected what madness there is in their companion, given the orderliness of his words and deeds?". It is also said: it is in the sense of الَّذِي, and on this view the speech proceeds from their [own] claim.

ukberi-tibyan:185-185.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَلَمْ يَنْظُرُوا فِي مَلَكُوتِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ وَأَنْ عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونَ قَدِ اقْتَرَبَ أَجَلُهُمْ فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَهُ يُؤْمِنُونَ) (١٨٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنْ عَسَى): it may be the lightened form (mukhaffafa) of the heavy [أَنَّ], and it may be maṣdariyya (infinitival); on both views it is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to مَلَكُوتِ. And (أَنْ يَكُونَ): the fāʿil (agent) of عَسَى; as for the noun of يَكُونَ, it is implied in it, and it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).
And (قَدِ اقْتَرَبَ أَجَلُهُمْ): in the accusative position as the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ; and the hāʾ in «بَعْدَهُ» is the pronoun of the Qurʾān.

ukberi-tibyan:186-186.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ وَيَذَرُهُمْ فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ) (١٨٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَلَا هَادِيَ): in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (وَيَذَرُهُمْ): in the nominative as a resumption, and in the jussive as conjoined to the position of «فَلَا هَادِيَ». It is also said: it was given sukūn because of the succession of vowels.

ukberi-tibyan:187-187.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ السَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرْسَاهَا قُلْ إِنَّمَا عِلْمُهَا عِنْدَ رَبِّي لَا يُجَلِّيهَا لِوَقْتِهَا إِلَّا هُوَ ثَقُلَتْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَا تَأْتِيكُمْ إِلَّا بَغْتَةً يَسْأَلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ عَنْهَا قُلْ إِنَّمَا عِلْمُهَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ) (١٨٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَيَّانَ): an indeclinable (mabnī) noun, because it contains [the meaning of] the interrogative particle, in the sense of مَتَى ("when?"); it is the khabar (predicate) of «مُرْسَاهَا». The clause is in the position of a genitive as a badal (substitute) from السَّاعَة, its implied form being "they ask you about the time of the arrival of
the Hour". And (مُرْسَاهَا): mufʿal from أَرْسَى; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like الْمُدْخَلُ and الْمُخْرَجُ in the sense of الْإِدْخَالُ and الْإِخْرَاجُ, i.e. "when will He set it in place?". (إِنَّمَا عِلْمُهَا): the maṣdar is put in construct with the object, and it is a mubtadaʾ (subject); and «عِنْدَ» is the khabar. (ثَقُلَتْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ): i.e. it weighs heavily on the people of the heavens and the earth, i.e. it will be heavy when it comes into being. It is also said that the implied form is "the knowledge of it weighs heavily on the people of the heavens". (حَفِيٌّ عَنْهَا): there are two views on it. One of them: its implied form is "they ask you about it as if you were حَفِيٌّ", i.e. concerned with seeking it; so He placed [عَنْهَا] before and [حَفِيٌّ] after. The second: «عَنْ» is in the sense of the bāʾ, i.e. حَفِيٌّ بِهَا ("well-informed of it"), and كَأَنَّكَ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object, and حَفِيٌّ is in the sense of مَحْفُوٌّ; it may also be faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil.

ukberi-tibyan:188-188.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ لَا أَمْلِكُ لِنَفْسِي نَفْعًا وَلَا ضَرًّا إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ وَلَوْ كُنْتُ أَعْلَمُ الْغَيْبَ لَاسْتَكْثَرْتُ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ وَمَا مَسَّنِيَ السُّوءُ إِنْ أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ وَبَشِيرٌ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ) (١٨٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِنَفْسِي): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَمْلِكُ, or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from نَفْعًا. (إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ): an exception from the same genus. (لِقَوْمٍ): it is attached to بَشِيرٌ according to the Basrans, and to نَذِيرٌ according to the Kufans.

ukberi-tibyan:189-189.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَجَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا لِيَسْكُنَ إِلَيْهَا فَلَمَّا تَغَشَّاهَا حَمَلَتْ حَمْلًا خَفِيفًا فَمَرَّتْ بِهِ فَلَمَّا أَثْقَلَتْ دَعَوَا اللَّهَ رَبَّهُمَا لَئِنْ آتَيْتَنَا صَالِحًا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ) (١٨٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمَرَّتْ بِهِ): it is read with shadda on the rāʾ, from الْمُرُورُ ("passing"); and مَارَتْ, with the alif and the rāʾ without shadda, from الْمَوْرُ, which is going and coming.

ukberi-tibyan:190-190.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا آتَاهُمَا صَالِحًا جَعَلَا لَهُ شُرَكَاءَ فِيمَا آتَاهُمَا فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ) (١٩٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَعَلَا لَهُ شُرَكَاءَ): it is read with the madd as a plural; and شِرْكًا, with kasra on the shīn, sukūn on the rāʾ and tanwīn. On this there are two views. One of them: its implied form is "they assigned to another than Him a share (شِرْك)", i.e. a portion. The second: "they assigned to Him a possessor of partnership"; so in both places the muḍāf was dropped.
